literature.headline_zh: 汉坦病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期汉坦病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 在自然测试集上,SEQC 仅使用 138 个可训练分类器参数就实现了 0.8833 准确率、0.7224 平衡准确率、0.7243 宏 F1、0.7740 ROC-AUC 和 0.5167 少数类 PR-AUC。 [10.1007/978-981-92-8119-0_8]
报道的心血管表现包括心肌损伤、心肌炎、心室功能障碍、心源性休克、心包受累、传导异常以及房性或室性心律失常。提出的机制包括内皮功能障碍、血管通透性增加、炎症和细胞因子激活、自主神经系统失调和微血管异常。 [10.4274/intercardiopers.2026.2026-8-5]
最终的 疫苗 构建体长度为 296 个氨基酸,表现出优异的抗原性 (0.7297)、非过敏性、结构稳定性和溶解性。疫苗 构建体的结构表明,94.6% 的残基位于 Ramachandran 图的首选区域,从而确保了良好的立体化学。分子对接和正常模式分析结果证实了疫苗构建体与TLR-3受体的稳定结合。 [10.1016/j.humimm.2026.112131]
maniculatus),尽管独立维护尚未得到证实;将适宜性与干旱气候和低强度发展联系起来的利基模型;2025 年新墨西哥州和加利福尼亚州的集群;首尔病毒感染与宠物鼠有关;以及游轮上的 2026 年安第斯山脉病毒 暴发,这再次引起了人们对人际传播汉坦病毒的关注。 [10.3390/zoonoticdis6040055]
现有文献描述了与汉坦病毒感染相关的一系列持续症状和急性神经并发症。这些后果包括疲劳、记忆力和注意力不集中、心理症状、睡眠障碍和生活质量受损,以及脑炎、精神状态改变和可逆性后部脑病综合征。然而,证据基础小且异构,限制了有关其频率、持续时间、机制和功能后果的结论。 [10.4081/mw.2026.83]

news.headline_zh: 汉坦病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期汉坦病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 据世界卫生组织(WHO)称,MV Hondius 号游轮上报告了疑似汉坦病毒暴发 病例,已确认三人死亡,一人在重症监护室。 [news-eba90930451ecac2]
本文讨论了汉坦病毒感染症状,重点是将早期 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 与常见季节性流感区分开来。它还提到了土耳其的新龙武器系统以及俄罗斯的政治和经济发展。 [news-2c671a5a7b25db76]
Hondius 号游轮上发生了一次 暴发 的 汉坦病毒,有证据表明存在人传人的 传播。科学家对暴发进行了分析,发现该病毒很可能是在船上传播的,并通过密切、长时间的接触在乘客之间传播。 [news-19291465d58e3458]
汉坦病毒 感染症状以及如何区分早期 HFRS 与常见季节性流感。 [news-f153692964c83791]
最近一艘游轮暴发被证实是汉坦病毒安第斯病毒株,据报告有3人死亡。专注于呼吸健康的出版商《呼吸治疗》报道了这一事件。 [news-fff4f30a91521ed4]

The article discusses hantavirus infection symptoms, focusing on distinguishing early hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) from common seasonal influenza. It also mentions Turkey's new Dragon weapon system and Russia's political and economic developments. [news-2c671a5a7b25db76]

An outbreak of hantavirus occurred on the cruise ship Hondius, with evidence suggesting human-to-human transmission. Scientists analyzed the outbreak and found that the virus was likely introduced on board and spread among passengers through close, prolonged contact. [news-19291465d58e3458]

papers.abstract: Pet rats represent a reservoir of multiple zoonotic pathogens. We demonstrated that pet rats, previously confirmed to be Seoul orthohantavirus-infected and involved in human infections in Germany, were concurrently infected with rat hepatitis E virus. The high degree of rat hepatitis E virus sequence identity suggests a single incursion event.

papers.title: Immunoinformatics based design and evaluation of a multi-epitope vaccine candidate targeting the envelopment polyprotein of Andes orthohantavirus
papers.abstract: Andes Orthohantavirus is known to be the etiological agent for hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), which is a highly dangerous disease with a very high death rate. There is no vaccine available to date to protect against this disease. This project aimed to develop a multi-epitope vaccine for Andes Orthohantavirus using immunoinformatics. Epitopes of CTL, HTL, and B cell types were predicted for the shortlisted Glycoprotein precursor after testing antigenicity, allergenicity, toxicity, and subcellular location. The chosen epitopes were combined using appropriate linkers and β-defensin as an adjuvant to create a multi-epitope vaccine. The final vaccine construct had a length of 296 amino acids and showed excellent antigenicity (0.7297), non-allergenicity, structural stability, and solubility properties. The structure of the vaccine construct showed that 94.6% of residues lie in the preferred areas of the Ramachandran plot, thus ensuring good stereochemistry. Molecular docking and normal mode analysis results confirmed the stable binding of the vaccine construct to TLR-3 receptors. At the same time, immune simulation revealed a fast degradation of antigens, production of antibodies, memory B-cells, and cytokines. In silico cloning integrated the codon-optimized gene with a CAI value of 0.97 and a GC percentage of 49.77% into the plasmid vector pET-28a(+). The designed multi-epitope vaccine displayed good predicted immunogenicity, structure, and expression properties that made it suitable to be used as a potential vaccine candidate against Andes Orthohantavirus infection. Further experimental validation is needed to assess its safety and effectiveness.

papers.source_body_en: Andes Orthohantavirus is known to be the etiological agent for hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS), which is a highly dangerous disease with a very high death rate. There is no vaccine available to date to protect against this disease. This project aimed to develop a multi-epitope vaccine for Andes Orthohantavirus using immunoinformatics. The designed multi-epitope vaccine displayed good predicted immunogenicity, structure, and expression properties that made it suitable to be used as a potential vaccine candidate against Andes Orthohantavirus infection. Further experimental validation is needed to assess its safety and effectiveness.

papers.title: Hantavirus Infections: Virology, Pathogenesis, Clinical Spectrum, and Emerging Therapeutic Frontiers
papers.abstract: Abstract Hantaviruses are rodent-borne zoonotic viruses that cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in Eurasia and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) in the Americas. Despite advances in hantavirus biology and clinical management, no universally approved antiviral therapy exists, and severe HPS remains associated with high mortality. This review summarizes the current understanding of hantavirus virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention, with emphasis on emerging therapeutic strategies. Hantavirus disease is characterized by profound vascular permeability despite limited direct cytopathic injury. Increasing evidence implicates immune-mediated endothelial dysfunction involving β3 integrins, CD8+ T-cell responses, angiopoietin/Tie2 dysregulation, vascular endothelial growth factor signaling, and neutrophil extracellular traps, thereby providing potential targets for antiviral and host-directed therapies. Clinical management remains predominantly supportive. Intravenous ribavirin may benefit patients when administered early in HFRS but has not demonstrated efficacy in established HPS. Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) has emerged as an important rescue therapy for severe HPS with cardiopulmonary collapse. Experimental approaches include favipiravir, direct-acting antivirals, convalescent plasma, broadly neutralizing monoclonal antibodies, viral entry and fusion inhibitors, and strategies targeting pathological host responses. Next-generation vaccine platforms, including DNA vaccines, virus-like particle, and structure-guided subunit vaccines, are under investigation. Integrating structural virology, antiviral discovery, immunology, genomic surveillance, and One Health approaches will be essential for developing effective therapeutic strategies.

source_records.abstract: Abstract Hantaviruses are rodent-borne zoonotic viruses that cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in Eurasia and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) in the Americas. Despite advances in hantavirus biology and clinical management, no universally approved antiviral therapy exists, and severe HPS remains associated with high mortality. This review summarizes the current understanding of hantavirus virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention, with emphasis on emerging therapeutic strategies. Hantavirus disease is characterized by profound vascular permeability despite limited direct cytopathic injury. Increasing evidence implicates immune-mediated endothelial dysfunction involving β3 integrins, CD8+ T-cell responses, angiopoietin/Tie2 dysregulation, vascular endothelial growth factor signaling, and neutrophil extracellular traps, thereby providing potential targets for antiviral and host-directed therapies. Experimental approaches include favipiravir, direct-acting antivirals, convalescent plasma, broadly neutralizing monoclonal antibodies, viral entry and fusion inhibitors, and strategies targeting pathological host responses. Next-generation vaccine platforms, including DNA vaccines, virus-like particle, and structure-guided subunit vaccines, are under investigation. Integrating structural virology, antiviral discovery, immunology, genomic surveillance, and One Health approaches will be essential for developing effective therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Hantavirus Transmission Dynamics in the United States: Reservoir Ecology, Environmental and Social Drivers, and Public Health Implications
papers.abstract: Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) is a rare but severe rodent-borne zoonosis. As of the end of 2023, the United States had recorded 890 laboratory-confirmed hantavirus cases since surveillance began in 1993, with 35% case fatality and 94% of cases west of the Mississippi River. This narrative review, searched through November 2026, synthesises epidemiological surveillance, reservoir ecology, ecological niche modelling, social-vulnerability analyses, and climate research to explain where and why Sin Nombre virus (SNV) spills over to people. We integrate evidence that SNV is detected in, and infectious virus isolated from, several rodent species beyond the western deer mouse (Peromyscus sonoriensis, formerly P. maniculatus), though independent maintenance is unproven; niche models linking suitability to arid climates and low-intensity development; the 2025 clusters in New Mexico and California; Seoul virus infections linked to pet rats; and the 2026 Andes virus outbreak on a cruise ship, which renewed attention to person-to-person-transmissible hantaviruses. We separate well-established findings from tentative, correlational inferences about biodiversity, social vulnerability, and climate change, and summarise clinical recognition and management. Priorities include taxonomy-aware rodent surveillance, integrated One Health forecasting, diagnosis and referral to centres offering extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, and targeted prevention for rural, Indigenous, and occupationally exposed communities.

papers.abstract_zh: 汉坦病毒肺综合征 (HPS) 是一种罕见但严重的啮齿动物传播的 人兽共患病。自1993年监测开始以来,截至2023年底,美国已记录了890例实验室确诊的汉坦病毒病例,病死率达35%,其中94%的病例发生在密西西比河以西。这篇叙述性综述检索至 2026 年 11 月,综合了流行病学 监测、储存宿主 生态学、生态位模型、社会脆弱性分析和气候研究,以解释 Sin Nombre 病毒 (SNV) 蔓延到人类的地点和原因。我们整合了证据,证明 SNV 在西部鹿鼠(Peromyscus sonoriensis,以前称为 P. maniculatus)以外的几种啮齿动物中检测到并分离出传染性病毒,尽管独立维持尚未得到证实;将适宜性与干旱气候和低强度发展联系起来的利基模型;2025 年新墨西哥州和加利福尼亚州的集群;首尔病毒感染与宠物鼠有关;以及游轮上的 2026 年安第斯山脉病毒 暴发,这再次引起了人们对人际传播汉坦病毒的关注。我们将公认的发现与有关生物多样性、社会脆弱性和气候变化的初步相关推论分开,并总结临床识别和管理。优先事项包括具有分类学意识的啮齿动物 监测、综合 One Health 预测、诊断 和转诊到提供体外膜氧合的中心,以及针对农村、土著和职业暴露社区的有针对性的预防。

papers.title: A systematic review of mental health and neuropsychiatric outcomes among survivors of hantavirus infection
papers.abstract: Hantavirus infections, including hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, can cause severe acute illness. Although survival has improved in some clinical settings, the mental health and neuropsychiatric outcomes associated with recovery remain insufficiently characterized. This systematic review synthesized the available evidence on mental health and neuropsychiatric outcomes associated with hantavirus infection, distinguishing persistent post-infectious symptoms from neurological complications occurring during acute illness. A systematic review was conducted with reference to PRISMA 2020 guidance. Electronic databases were searched for eligible studies published between 2005 and 2025. Methodological quality was evaluated using Joanna Briggs Institute appraisal tools, and findings were synthesized narratively because of substantial heterogeneity in study designs, populations, follow-up periods, and outcome assessment. Nine studies were included. Reported outcomes fell into two broad clinical categories. The first comprised persistent or follow-up symptoms, including fatigue, memory and concentration difficulties, psychological symptoms, sleep disturbances, and impaired quality of life. These outcomes were described in studies examining recovery after HCPS and Puumala virus-associated nephropathia epidemica. The second category comprised neurological complications, including encephalitis, altered mental status, and posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome. These acute manifestations were interpreted separately from persistent post-infectious outcomes because their occurrence during acute illness does not establish long-term neuropsychiatric impairment. Differences in study design, sample size, follow-up duration, and outcome assessment limited direct comparisons and prevented reliable estimates of population-level prevalence. The available literature describes a range of persistent symptoms and acute neurological complications associated with hantavirus infection. However, the small and heterogeneous evidence base limits conclusions regarding their frequency, duration, mechanisms, and functional consequences. Larger longitudinal studies using standardized assessments and appropriate comparison groups are needed to clarify recovery trajectories and inform follow-up care.

papers.abstract_zh: 汉坦病毒 感染,包括汉坦病毒心肺综合征 (HCPS) 和 肾综合征出血热,可导致严重的急性疾病。尽管在某些临床环境中生存率有所改善,但与康复相关的心理健康和神经精神结果仍不充分。这项系统评价综合了与汉坦病毒感染相关的心理健康和神经精神结局的现有证据,区分了持续的感染后症状和急性疾病期间发生的神经系统并发症。参考 PRISMA 2020 指南进行了系统审查。我们在电子数据库中搜索了 2005 年至 2025 年间发表的符合条件的研究。使用乔安娜·布里格斯研究所评估工具评估了方法学质量,由于研究设计、人群、随访期和结果评估存在显着异质性,因此对研究结果进行了叙述性综合。纳入了九项研究。报告的结果分为两大临床类别。第一个包括持续或后续症状,包括疲劳、记忆力和注意力困难、心理症状、睡眠障碍和生活质量受损。这些结果在检查 HCPS 和普马拉病毒相关流行性肾病后恢复情况的研究中得到了描述。第二类包括神经系统并发症,包括脑炎、精神状态改变和可逆性后部脑病综合征。这些急性表现与持续的感染后结果分开解释,因为它们在急性疾病期间的发生并不会造成长期的神经精神损害。研究设计、样本量、随访持续时间和结果评估的差异限制了直接比较,并阻碍了对人群水平 患病率 的可靠估计。现有文献描述了与汉坦病毒感染相关的一系列持续症状和急性神经并发症。然而,证据基础小且异构,限制了有关其频率、持续时间、机制和功能后果的结论。需要使用标准化评估和适当的比较组进行更大规模的纵向研究,以阐明恢复轨迹并为后续护理提供信息。

analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 研究设计、样本量、随访持续时间和结果评估的差异限制了直接比较,并阻碍了对人群水平 患病率 的可靠估计。The heterogeneity in the evidence base also prevents drawing definitive conclusions about the long-term neuropsychiatric effects of汉坦病毒infection.
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要使用标准化评估和适当的比较组进行更大规模的纵向研究,以阐明恢复轨迹并为后续护理提供信息。这将有助于更好地理解持续感染后症状和急性神经并发症的功能后果和机制。

papers.full_text: Abstract Host classification from viral genomic sequences is challenging because biologically meaningful signals must be extracted from high-dimensional sequence data under strong class imbalance. This paper presents a hybrid quantum machine learning framework for binary human versus non-human host classification. Raw nucleotide sequences are first encoded using a frozen DNABERT-2 model and compressed into bounded low-dimensional latent vectors through a bottleneck autoencoder. These quantum-compatible features are then classified using the proposed Segment-Aware Entangled Quantum Classifier (SEQC), a compact variational quantum decision module with trainable dual-angle encoding, data re-uploading, segment-aware local-to-global entanglement, global mixing, and trainable observable readout. Experiments are conducted in a leakage-safe, resource-controlled simulation setting: classifier training uses a balanced subset of samples, while validation, threshold tuning, and testing are performed on the full natural imbalanced splits. On the natural test set, SEQC achieves \(0.8833\) accuracy, \(0.7224\) balanced accuracy, \(0.7243\) macro-F1, \(0.7740\) ROC-AUC, and \(0.5167\) minority-class PR-AUC using only \(138\) trainable classifier parameters. Comparisons with classical baselines show that SEQC is competitive as a compact nonlinear decision module, particularly in minority-class ranking. Ablation studies further indicate that encoding choice, bottleneck dimension, and entanglement structure should be matched to the supplied latent representation. papers.title_original: Segment-Aware Entangled Quantum Classifier for Imbalanced Hantavirus Host Prediction

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenge of host classification from viral genomic sequences, particularly in the context of imbalanced data, which is critical for understanding hantavirus transmission and pathogenesis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study presents a hybrid quantum machine learning framework for binary human versus non-human host classification, using a balanced subset of samples for training and full natural imbalanced splits for validation, threshold tuning, and testing.
analysis.methods: Raw nucleotide sequences are encoded using a frozen DNABERT-2 model and compressed into low-dimensional latent vectors through a bottleneck autoencoder. These quantum-compatible features are then classified using the Segment-Aware Entangled Quantum Classifier (SEQC), which incorporates trainable dual-angle encoding, data re-uploading, segment-aware local-to-global entanglement, global mixing, and trainable observable readout.
analysis.main_results: On the natural test set, SEQC achieved 0.8833 accuracy, 0.7224 balanced accuracy, 0.7243 macro-F1, 0.7740 ROC-AUC, and 0.5167 minority-class PR-AUC using only 138 trainable classifier parameters.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that SEQC is competitive as a compact nonlinear decision module, particularly in minority-class ranking, and highlight its novelty as a framework tailored for imbalanced data in host prediction.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more accurate and efficient methods for predicting hantavirus hosts, which is crucial for surveillance, risk assessment, and prevention strategies in public health.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a simulation setting, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of real-world validation and potential generalizability issues.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a hybrid quantum machine learning framework called the Segment-Aware Entangled Quantum Classifier (SEQC) for predicting hantavirus hosts from genomic sequences. The research addresses the challenge of extracting biologically meaningful signals from high-dimensional and imbalanced sequence data, which is essential for understanding hantavirus transmission and pathogenesis. The framework uses a frozen DNABERT-2 model to encode raw nucleotide sequences and compresses them into low-dimensional latent vectors via a bottleneck autoencoder. These features are then classified using SEQC, which incorporates quantum-compatible techniques such as trainable dual-angle encoding, data re-uploading, and segment-aware entanglement. On the natural test set, SEQC achieved 0.8833 accuracy, 0.7224 balanced accuracy, 0.7243 macro-F1, 0.7740 ROC-AUC, and 0.5167 minority-class PR-AUC using only 138 trainable parameters. The authors interpret that SEQC is competitive in minority-class ranking, offering a novel approach for imbalanced data in host prediction. The findings have implications for improving surveillance and risk assessment for hantavirus infections. However, the study is limited to a simulation setting, which may affect its generalizability and real-world applicability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决从病毒基因组序列中进行 宿主 分类的挑战,特别是在数据不平衡的情况下,这对于理解汉坦病毒传播 和 发病机制 至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究提出了一种混合量子机器学习框架,用于人类与非人类 宿主 分类,使用平衡的样本子集进行训练,并使用完全自然的不平衡分割进行验证、阈值调整和测试。
elements_zh.methods: 原始核苷酸序列使用冷冻 DNABERT-2 模型进行编码,并通过瓶颈自动编码器压缩为低维潜在 媒介。然后使用分段感知纠缠量子分类器 (SEQC) 对这些量子兼容特征进行分类,该分类器结合了可训练的双角度编码、数据重新上传、分段感知的局部到全局纠缠、全局混合和可训练的可观察读数。
elements_zh.main_results: 在自然测试集上,SEQC 仅使用 138 个可训练分类器参数就实现了 0.8833 准确率、0.7224 平衡准确率、0.7243 宏 F1、0.7740 ROC-AUC 和 0.5167 少数类 PR-AUC。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,SEQC 作为紧凑的非线性决策模块具有竞争力,特别是在少数群体排名中,并强调了它作为针对 宿主 预测中不平衡数据量身定制的框架的新颖性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为开发更准确、更有效的方法来预测汉坦病毒宿主 提供信息,这对于公共卫生领域的 监测、风险评估和预防策略至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于模拟环境,由于缺乏现实世界的验证和潜在的普遍性问题,证据强度中等。

Abstract Host classification from viral genomic sequences is challenging because biologically meaningful signals must be extracted from high-dimensional sequence data under strong class imbalance. This paper presents a hybrid quantum machine learning framework for binary human versus non-human host classification. Raw nucleotide sequences are first encoded using a frozen DNABERT-2 model and compressed into bounded low-dimensional latent vectors through a bottleneck autoencoder. These quantum-compatible features are then classified using the proposed Segment-Aware Entangled Quantum Classifier (SEQC), a compact variational quantum decision module with trainable dual-angle encoding, data re-uploading, segment-aware local-to-global entanglement, global mixing, and trainable observable readout. Experiments are conducted in a leakage-safe, resource-controlled simulation setting: classifier training uses a balanced subset of samples, while validation, threshold tuning, and testing are performed on the full natural imbalanced splits. analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决从病毒基因组序列中进行 宿主 分类的挑战,特别是在数据不平衡的情况下,这对于理解汉坦病毒传播 和 发病机制 至关重要。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究提出了一种混合量子机器学习框架,用于人类与非人类 宿主 分类,使用平衡的样本子集进行训练,并使用完全自然的不平衡分割进行验证、阈值调整和测试。
analysis_zh.methods: 原始核苷酸序列使用冷冻 DNABERT-2 模型进行编码,并通过瓶颈自动编码器压缩为低维潜在 媒介。然后使用分段感知纠缠量子分类器 (SEQC) 对这些量子兼容特征进行分类,该分类器结合了可训练的双角度编码、数据重新上传、分段感知的局部到全局纠缠、全局混合和可训练的可观察读数。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在自然测试集上,SEQC 仅使用 138 个可训练分类器参数就实现了 0.8833 准确率、0.7224 平衡准确率、0.7243 宏 F1、0.7740 ROC-AUC 和 0.5167 少数类 PR-AUC。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,SEQC 作为紧凑的非线性决策模块具有竞争力,特别是在少数群体排名中,并强调了它作为针对 宿主 预测中不平衡数据量身定制的框架的新颖性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为开发更准确、更有效的方法来预测汉坦病毒宿主 提供信息,这对于公共卫生领域的 监测、风险评估和预防策略至关重要。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于模拟环境,由于缺乏现实世界的验证和潜在的普遍性问题,证据强度中等。

papers.full_text: Abstract Hantavirus infection can lead to hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, and cardiovascular (CV) involvement is increasingly recognized as an important feature of severe disease. The present review summarizes the epidemiology, clinical manifestations, pathophysiological mechanisms, diagnostic evaluation, and management of CV involvement in hantavirus infection. The available evidence includes experimental studies, observational cohorts, case series, and clinical reports. Reported CV manifestations include myocardial injury, myocarditis, ventricular dysfunction, cardiogenic shock, pericardial involvement, conduction abnormalities, and atrial or ventricular arrhythmias. Proposed mechanisms include endothelial dysfunction, increased vascular permeability, inflammatory and cytokine activation, autonomic nervous system dysregulation, and microvascular abnormalities. Clinical assessment may reveal hypotension, elevated cardiac biomarkers, ventricular dysfunction, and circulatory collapse. Echocardiography, cardiac biomarker assessment, electrocardiography, speckle-tracking echocardiography, and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging may aid diagnosis and risk stratification. Management is largely supportive and may include individualized fluid management, vasopressors and inotropes as needed, hemodynamic monitoring, and mechanical circulatory support or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation for refractory shock. The current evidence base is limited by the predominance of observational data and heterogeneity in diagnostic and follow-up strategies. Prospective studies are needed to clarify the mechanisms of myocardial injury, identify prognostic biomarkers, and establish evidence-based approaches to CV assessment and management. Keywords: Arrhythmia, capillary leak syndrome, cardiogenic shock, endothelial dysfunction, myocarditis INTRODUCTION Hantaviruses are zoonotic, enveloped viruses with negative-sense, single-stranded RNA genomes belonging to the family Hantaviridae. Rodents serve as their natural reservoirs, and humans become infected by inhaling aerosols containing infected rodent excreta. Hantavirus infections are a global public health concern and can cause severe disease. Their geographic distribution is closely associated with the distribution of their reservoir species. In Europe and Asia, hantavirus infections typically manifest as hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS), whereas in the Americas, the most common presentation is hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS). HFRS is characterized by fever, thrombocytopenia, vascular leakage, and renal failure, whereas HCPS is primarily associated with pulmonary edema, respiratory failure, and circulatory collapse. Despite differences in their clinical presentations, both syndromes are associated with increased vascular permeability and endothelial dysfunction.1-3 Research on hantavirus infection has traditionally focused on its pulmonary and renal manifestations. However, accumulating evidence suggests that cardiovascular (CV) involvement may also contribute to disease severity and clinical outcomes. Reported CV manifestations range from mild myocardial injury and hemodynamic abnormalities to myocarditis, ventricular dysfunction, arrhythmias, cardiogenic shock, and, rarely, sudden cardiac death. The CV effects of hantavirus infection may involve endothelial activation, capillary leakage, systemic inflammation, and hemodynamic disturbances. Nevertheless, the mechanisms underlying CV involvement and the extent to which individual mechanisms contribute to clinical outcomes remain poorly understood. Accordingly, this review examines the pathophysiological mechanisms, clinical manifestations, diagnostic approaches, and therapeutic implications of hantavirus-associated CV involvement.4-6 Citation Strategy Citations were reassessed throughout the manuscript to improve the alignment between individual statements and their supporting sources. Hantavirus-specific and CV references were prioritized for claims concerning CV manifestations, myocardial injury, hemodynamic abnormalities, imaging, biomarkers, and clinical outcomes. Broader reviews and general critical care or CV sources were retained primarily to support general concepts and management principles when hantavirus-specific evidence was limited. Duplicate citations were reduced where appropriate, and citation placement was reviewed to ensure that each reference supports the corresponding statement. Literature Review Methodology This article is a narrative review. The relevant literature was identified through a focused search of the biomedical literature using combinations of the following terms: “hantavirus,” “hantavirus infection,” “hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome,” “hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome,” “cardiovascular,” “cardiac,” “myocarditis,” “heart failure,” “shock,” “arrhythmia,” “echocardiography,” “speckle-tracking echocardiography,” “cardiac magnetic resonance,” “biomarkers,” and “extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.” Original research articles, observational studies, case series, case reports, reviews, and guideline or consensus documents were considered based on their relevance to the CV manifestations, mechanisms of injury, diagnostic evaluation, management, and long-term outcomes of hantavirus infection. The reference lists of relevant publications were also screened to identify additional studies. Because this was a narrative review, no formal systematic review protocol, meta-analysis, or quantitative risk-of-bias assessment was undertaken. The available evidence was critically appraised, with particular attention to the predominantly observational nature of the published literature and the methodological heterogeneity among studies. Host and Viral Responses Hantaviruses are enveloped viruses with negative-sense, single-stranded RNA genomes belonging to the family Hantaviridae. Hantavirus genomes are tripartite and consist of three segments (S, M, and L) that encode the nucleocapsid protein, the envelope glycoproteins (Gn and Gc), and the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. The envelope glycoproteins are involved in viral attachment to and entry into host cells, whereas the nucleocapsid protein plays a role in viral replication and interactions with host immune responses. Hantaviruses are transmitted by rodents, with each viral species typically associated with a specific rodent reservoir. Infected animals may shed the virus in their urine, feces, and saliva, resulting in environmental contamination and subsequent aerosol transmission to humans. South American hantavirus strains are associated with HCPS, and person-to-person transmission has been reported for some strains.7,8 Hantavirus glycoproteins interact with β3 integrins expressed on endothelial and other vascular cells, platelets, and additional cell types. Following receptor-mediated entry, viral replication takes place in the cytoplasm. Endothelial involvement is associated with increased vascular permeability and capillary leakage, both of which are prominent features of severe disease. Available evidence suggests that host immune responses are major determinants of disease severity. Although hantaviruses are generally considered non-cytopathic, infection can activate T-cells, macrophages, and natural killer cells. Endothelial dysfunction and increased vascular permeability have been associated with inflammatory mediators, including tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin (IL)-6, and interferon-γ. Severe hantavirus infection may therefore be accompanied by cardiac and hemodynamic abnormalities, although the relative contributions of immune-mediated mechanisms remain incompletely understood.9,10 Pathophysiology of CV Injury CV involvement in hantavirus infection likely results from interactions among viral infection, endothelial dysfunction, immune dysregulation, and hemodynamic disturbances. Experimental and pathological observations suggest that hantaviruses predominantly affect vascular endothelial cells rather than cardiomyocytes. Systemic inflammatory responses have also been reported. Together, these processes have been proposed to contribute to ventricular dysfunction, arrhythmias, circulatory collapse, and multiorgan dysfunction.11 Endothelial Dysfunction Endothelial dysfunction is a well-recognized feature of severe hantavirus infection. The effects of viral particles on endothelial cells may be mediated through mechanisms that are not directly related to cytolysis. Endothelial dysregulation may lead to the disruption of intercellular junctions, increased vascular permeability, and impaired regulation of vascular tone. Experimental studies show that hantavirus glycoproteins bind to β3 integrins and disrupt endothelial signaling and barrier function. Endothelial barrier dysfunction has also been linked to permeability mediators such as vascular endothelial growth factor and angiopoietins. These pathological changes may cause hypotension, tissue edema, and reduced organ perfusion.12 Capillary Leak Syndrome Severe hantavirus infection is characterized by CV instability and capillary leak syndrome. Increased endothelial permeability allows proteins and fluid to extravasate into the interstitial space, causing tissue edema and intravascular volume depletion. In HCPS, pulmonary capillary leakage may lead to pulmonary edema and profound hypoxia. Reduced effective intravascular volume may also cause hypotension and shock secondary to reduced cardiac preload. Severe capillary leakage may further impair ventricular filling and oxygen delivery to myocardial cells, thereby contributing to reduced ventricular function. The extent of vascular leakage has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes.13 Cytokine Activation and Inflammation Inflammatory pathways are considered important contributors to CV involvement in hantavirus infection. Proinflammatory cytokines, such as TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-8, and interferon-γ, have been reported in clinical and experimental studies. The upregulation of these cytokines has been associated with increased endothelial permeability, leukocyte recruitment, and vascular inflammation. Inflammatory mediators may also exert negative inotropic effects. For example, TNF-α and IL-6 have been associated with abnormalities in calcium handling, reduced myocardial contractility, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Transient myocardial dysfunction has been reported in severe hantavirus infection, and cytokine-mediated myocardial depression has been proposed as one of the mechanisms contributing to this finding.14 Pathogenesis of Myocardial Injury Myocardial injury in hantavirus infection likely has a multifactorial etiology. Current evidence suggests that immune-mediated and endothelial mechanisms may contribute to myocardial injury, whereas the extent of direct cardiomyocyte infection remains uncertain. Myocarditis has not been characterized in detail in patients with hantavirus infection. However, clinicopathological findings suggestive of myocarditis have been reported in some cases, along with ventricular dysfunction and elevated cardiac troponin levels. Cytokines are thought to contribute to myocardial depression, although microvascular dysfunction, systemic hypoperfusion, oxidative stress, and inflammatory cell infiltration may also play a role. These processes may lead to myocardial dysfunction, myocarditis, and cardiogenic shock in susceptible patients. The recovery of ventricular function reported in many cases suggests that reversible functional impairment may predominate over irreversible myocyte injury in at least some patients.15 The proposed pathophysiological mechanisms linking hantavirus infection to CV injury and their potential clinical consequences are illustrated in . Microvascular Dysfunction Microvascular dysfunction has been proposed as an additional mechanism contributing to CV involvement in hantavirus infection. Microcirculatory blood flow may be compromised by endothelial and complement activation, inflammatory cytokines, and coagulopathy. Increased vascular permeability and interstitial edema may increase the diffusion distance for oxygen, while platelet activation and local thrombus formation may further impair microvascular perfusion. These abnormalities may impair myocardial perfusion even in the presence of minimal epicardial coronary artery disease. Microvascular dysfunction has therefore been proposed as a potential contributor to myocardial ischemia, ventricular dysfunction, arrhythmias, and hemodynamic deterioration. Systemic microcirculatory impairment may also contribute to multiorgan dysfunction. However, the relative importance of these mechanisms and their prognostic significance in hantavirus infection remain incompletely established.16 The pathophysiological processes outlined above-including endothelial dysfunction, capillary leakage, systemic inflammation, myocardial injury, and microvascular abnormalities-provide a plausible basis for the range of CV manifestations reported in hantavirus infection. These processes may manifest clinically as transient hemodynamic disturbances, subclinical myocardial injury, overt ventricular dysfunction, myocarditis, arrhythmias, or cardiogenic shock. Understanding the links between these underlying mechanisms and their clinical consequences is important for recognizing and managing CV involvement. The next section therefore examines the principal CV manifestations reported in patients with hantavirus infection.16 CV Manifestations CV manifestations are increasingly recognized as contributors to morbidity and mortality in hantavirus infection. Although pulmonary and renal complications have been studied more extensively, CV involvement is an important feature of severe HCPS. The clinical spectrum ranges from mild hemodynamic abnormalities to severe ventricular dysfunction and circulatory collapse. Endothelial dysfunction, increased vascular permeability, systemic inflammation, and myocardial injury have been implicated in the CV manifestations of severe disease.17 Shock and Hypotension Hypotension is a common CV manifestation of severe hantavirus infection. Inflammatory mediators induce vasodilation, leading to decreased systemic vascular resistance, while increased vascular permeability causes plasma leakage into the tissues and reduces effective intravascular volume. Consequently, shock may be hypovolemic, distributive, cardiogenic, or mixed. In patients with significant myocardial dysfunction, fluid therapy may exacerbate pulmonary edema and hemodynamic instability. Persistent hypotension should prompt a comprehensive hemodynamic evaluation and the initiation of vasopressor support, as indicated.18 Myocarditis Myocarditis has been reported in patients with HFRS and HCPS, although its frequency and clinical significance remain uncertain. Clinical features have included chest pain, electrocardiographic changes, elevated cardiac biomarkers, and reversible ventricular dysfunction. Histopathological analyses have revealed interstitial inflammatory infiltrates, myocardial edema, and focal myocyte injury. In patients with suspected myocarditis, cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging may demonstrate myocardial edema and late gadolinium enhancement. Immune-mediated mechanisms and cytokine-associated myocardial depression have been proposed, although direct viral injury to the myocardium cannot be excluded. Ventricular function appears to recover in many patients after the acute illness.15 Pericardial Involvement Pericardial involvement appears to be less common than myocardial dysfunction but has been reported in patients with hantavirus infection. Acute pericarditis may present with chest pain and electrocardiographic changes, whereas echocardiography may reveal a small pericardial effusion. Pericardial abnormalities may develop in the setting of systemic inflammation and increased vascular permeability. Although clinically significant cardiac tamponade appears to be rare, hemodynamic deterioration should prompt echocardiographic assessment. Echocardiography is useful for diagnosing and monitoring pericardial involvement.19,20 Acute Heart Failure Severe hantavirus infection may be complicated by acute heart failure. Rapid-onset ventricular dysfunction has been associated with myocardial inflammation, cytokine-mediated myocardial depression, microvascular abnormalities, and acute changes in ventricular loading conditions. Clinical features may include dyspnea, pulmonary congestion, elevated natriuretic peptide concentrations, and reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). In HCPS, acute ventricular dysfunction may contribute to pulmonary edema and complicate the differentiation of cardiogenic from non-cardiogenic respiratory failure. In some patients, transient inflammatory and hemodynamic disturbances may play a greater role than irreversible structural myocardial damage.15 Right Ventricular Dysfunction Right ventricular dysfunction may be underrecognized in severe hantavirus infection. Pulmonary edema, hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction, and pulmonary vascular abnormalities may increase right ventricular afterload. Echocardiography in critically ill patients may reveal right ventricular enlargement associated with impaired function or elevated pulmonary artery pressure. Because right ventricular function is essential for maintaining cardiac output, significant right ventricular dysfunction may contribute to hemodynamic deterioration. A comprehensive echocardiographic examination should therefore include an assessment of right ventricular size and systolic function.21 Cardiogenic Shock Cardiogenic shock is a severe manifestation of CV involvement in HCPS and has been associated with high mortality in reported cohorts. The relevant literature was identified through a focused search of the biomedical literature using combinations of the following terms: “hantavirus,” “hantavirus infection,” “hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome,” “hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome,” “cardiovascular,” “cardiac,” “myocarditis,” “heart failure,” “shock,” “arrhythmia,” “echocardiography,” “speckle-tracking echocardiography,” “cardiac magnetic resonance,” “biomarkers,” and “extracorporeal membrane oxygenation.” Original research articles, observational studies, case series, case reports, reviews, and guideline or consensus documents were considered based on their relevance to the CV manifestations, mechanisms of injury, diagnostic evaluation, management, and long-term outcomes of hantavirus infection. The reference lists of relevant publications were also screened to identify additional studies. Because this was a narrative review, no formal systematic review protocol, meta-analysis, or quantitative risk-of-bias assessment was undertaken. The available evidence was critically appraised, with particular attention to the predominantly observational nature of the published literature and the methodological heterogeneity among studies. Host and Viral Responses Hantaviruses are enveloped viruses with negative-sense, single-stranded RNA genomes belonging to the family Hantaviridae. Hantavirus genomes are tripartite and consist of three segments (S, M, and L) that encode the nucleocapsid protein, the envelope glycoproteins (Gn and Gc), and the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. The envelope glycoproteins are involved in viral attachment to and entry into host cells, whereas the nucleocapsid protein plays a role in viral replication and interactions with host immune responses. Hantaviruses are transmitted by rodents, with each viral species typically associated with a specific rodent reservoir. Infected animals may shed the virus in their urine, feces, and saliva, resulting in environmental contamination and subsequent aerosol transmission to humans. South American hantavirus strains are associated with HCPS, and person-to-person transmission has been reported for some strains.7,8 Hantavirus glycoproteins interact with β3 integrins expressed on endothelial and other vascular cells, platelets, and additional cell types. Following receptor-mediated entry, viral replication takes place in the cytoplasm. Endothelial involvement is associated with increased vascular permeability and capillary leakage, both of which are prominent features of severe disease. Available evidence suggests that host immune responses are major determinants of disease severity. Although hantaviruses are generally considered non-cytopathic, infection can activate T-cells, macrophages, and natural killer cells. Endothelial dysfunction and increased vascular permeability have been associated with inflammatory mediators, including tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin (IL)-6, and interferon-γ. analysis.research_question_and_background: This review aimed to summarize the epidemiology, clinical manifestations, pathophysiological mechanisms, diagnostic evaluation, and management of cardiovascular involvement in hantavirus infection, as CV involvement is increasingly recognized as an important feature of severe disease.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a review of the available evidence, which includes experimental studies, observational cohorts, case series, and clinical reports. It covers hantavirus infections in humans, particularly focusing on cardiovascular manifestations.
analysis.methods: The review synthesized data from experimental studies, observational cohorts, case series, and clinical reports, which were used to identify reported cardiovascular manifestations and proposed mechanisms of disease.
analysis.main_results: Reported cardiovascular manifestations include myocardial injury, myocarditis, ventricular dysfunction, cardiogenic shock, pericardial involvement, conduction abnormalities, and atrial or ventricular arrhythmias. Proposed mechanisms include endothelial dysfunction, increased vascular permeability, inflammatory and cytokine activation, autonomic nervous system dysregulation, and microvascular abnormalities.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that cardiovascular involvement may contribute to disease severity and clinical outcomes, highlighting the need for further research to clarify mechanisms and improve management strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform the development of more accurate diagnostic tools and targeted management approaches for cardiovascular complications in hantavirus infections, which are a global public health concern.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by the predominance of observational data and heterogeneity in diagnostic and follow-up strategies, which may affect the generalizability of findings. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This review provides an overview of cardiovascular involvement in hantavirus infection, emphasizing its role in disease severity. It highlights the clinical manifestations such as myocardial injury, myocarditis, and cardiogenic shock, as well as proposed mechanisms like endothelial dysfunction and vascular permeability. The study underscores the importance of cardiovascular assessment in hantavirus infections and suggests that supportive management strategies, including individualized fluid management and hemodynamic monitoring, may be necessary. However, the evidence is primarily observational and heterogeneous, limiting the strength of conclusions. The findings have implications for improving diagnostic and therapeutic approaches in managing cardiovascular complications associated with hantavirus infections.

papers.full_text: nature immunology Volume 27 | December 2026 | 2357–2359 | 2357 Vaccine preparedness for the next emerging infectious disease crisis Florian Krammer Recent outbreaks with viruses such as Bundi­bugyo virus and Andes virus are a reminder that another pandemic can happen at any time. This Comment summarizes where we stand with pandemic preparedness from a vaccine perspective. During the COVID-19 pandemic, we witnessed vaccine develop­ment at its finest. Vaccines against the novel coronavirus SARS-CoV-2 were developed at record speed and were made available within approximately 1 year after the outbreak started1. This swift devel­ opment of vaccines was facilitated by new technologies such as the mRNA vaccine platform2 but also by a wealth of exist­ ing knowledge because of many years of virology, vacci­nology and structural biology research. Much has happened since the COVID-19 pandemic. Technology has evolved, new insights into mechanisms of protection and basic immunology have been gained and regulatory and policy views have changed (Fig. 1), especially in the USA. Where does this leave us with vaccine preparedness for emerging pathogens? Mucosal immunity matters A clear lesson learned from the COVID-19 pandemic was that intramus­ cular vaccination can only imperfectly protect from infection with respiratory viruses per se and from onward transmission1. Vaccines that are administered via mucosal surfaces may be a better option to induce immunity in the upper respiratory tract to protect from infection with respiratory viruses. This was clearly identified as a gap, and funding agencies, including the US National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) and Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA), set out to support the development of mucosal vaccine approaches for COVID-19 (ref. 3). Unfortunately, funding for many of these vaccines was terminated or redirected to other projects owing to the policy decision that COVID-19 is no longer a priority. How­ ever, having infection- and transmission-blocking vaccines early in an outbreak with a respiratory virus would notably increase the effect of vaccines. Although several intranasal vaccines for COVID-19 are either still in development or already licensed outside the USA and Europe4,5, there is a large gap in terms of vaccine preparedness when it comes to mucosal vaccination routes. Having mucosal vaccines with clear immunological (and potentially mucosal) correlates of protection and established vaccine efficacy and safety on the market would increase confidence in these vaccine platforms and would likely enable early deployment during an outbreak or a pandemic. Broadly protective or strain-specific vaccines Studies of influenza virus and HIV-1 have shown that RNA viruses can evolve quickly. This was also observed with SARS-CoV-2. With the emergence of the Omicron variants, vaccines had to be updated to stay effective. However, updating vaccines to respond to emerging variants means always being one step behind the virus. This is a scenario with which we are very familiar from influenza virus vaccines. Owing to the antigenic variability of RNA viruses, the development of broadly protective vaccines has been the focus in the HIV-1 and influenza fields for many years but also became an important topic for SARS-CoV-2. The concept of broadly protective vaccines goes further than the idea of covering evolving virus variants. The idea has expanded to develop vaccines that potentially can protect from whole virus families, which would considerably increase pandemic preparedness. Although fund­ ing for such vaccines has been made available (for example, via the NIAID Collaborative Influenza Vaccine Innovation Centers program, the BARDA funding initiatives and the European Health and Digital Executive Agency), they have not progressed far enough to be used in case of an emergency. Further investment is urgently needed to advance these candidates and concepts through clinical development and real­ ize their potential as tools to combat evolving viral threats and future Comment https://doi.org/10.1038/s41590-026-02726-w Check for updates Broadly protective vs virus/strain- specific vaccines Mucosal vs injected vaccines Vaccine platform Vaccine acceptance Market Regulatory policy Manufacturing speed Funding policy Basic research Vaccine preparedness Vaccine Fig. 1 | Factors and aspects that influence epidemic and pandemic vaccine preparedness. Technology has advanced, our understanding of virus biology has markedly increased and COVID- 19 has shown us that vaccines can be developed quickly if needed and if an effort is made by all stakeholders. However, there is much still to learn; from basic research and clinical testing to manufacturing and regulatory policies. Importantly, funding policies and regulatory policies are changing in parts of the world, partially influenced by the anti-vaccine movement that now has advocates within governments. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need for improved vaccine preparedness against emerging infectious diseases, particularly highlighting the importance of mucosal immunity in protecting against respiratory viruses. The background emphasizes the lessons learned from the COVID-19 pandemic, where intramuscular vaccination had limited effectiveness in preventing infection and transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a commentary that summarizes the current state of pandemic preparedness from a vaccine development perspective. It discusses the evolution of vaccine technologies, insights into immunological mechanisms, and changes in regulatory and policy approaches since the COVID-19 pandemic, with a focus on respiratory viruses.
analysis.methods: The methods section is not explicitly detailed in the provided evidence, but the commentary outlines the use of new technologies such as mRNA platforms and references studies on influenza virus and HIV-1 to highlight the challenges of developing broadly protective or strain-specific vaccines for RNA viruses.
analysis.main_results: The main results include the observation that intramuscular vaccination only imperfectly protects against respiratory virus infection and transmission. It also notes that several intranasal vaccines for COVID-19 are either in development or licensed outside the USA and Europe, but there remains a significant gap in mucosal vaccine preparedness.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that mucosal vaccines could offer better protection against respiratory viruses, especially if they have clear immunological correlates of protection and established efficacy and safety. This interpretation is novel in its emphasis on the potential of mucosal vaccination routes for future pandemic preparedness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that developing mucosal vaccines with proven immunological correlates could enhance preparedness for future respiratory virus outbreaks, allowing for more effective early deployment and potentially reducing the spread of infection.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a commentary and does not present original data, which limits its evidence strength. However, it draws on existing knowledge and references to provide a high-level overview of current vaccine preparedness challenges and opportunities.

analysis.summary_en: This commentary discusses the importance of mucosal immunity in protecting against respiratory viruses, highlighting the limitations of intramuscular vaccination observed during the COVID-19 pandemic. It emphasizes the need for mucosal vaccines with clear immunological correlates of protection and established efficacy and safety. The study also notes that while several intranasal vaccines for COVID-19 are in development or licensed outside the USA and Europe, there remains a significant gap in mucosal vaccine preparedness. The findings suggest that such vaccines could improve pandemic preparedness by enabling early deployment and reducing transmission. However, the commentary lacks original data and is based on existing knowledge, which limits its evidence strength.

elements_zh.methods: 所提供的证据中没有明确详细说明方法部分,但评论概述了 mRNA 平台等新技术的使用以及流感病毒和 HIV-1 的参考研究,以强调开发针对 RNA 病毒的广泛保护性或毒株特异性 疫苗 的挑战。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,粘膜 疫苗 可以提供更好的针对呼吸道病毒的保护,特别是如果它们具有明确的免疫学保护相关性并已确定的功效和安全性。这种解释的新颖之处在于它强调了粘膜 疫苗接种 途径在未来大流行防范方面的潜力。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,开发具有已证实的免疫相关性的粘膜 疫苗 可以增强对未来呼吸道病毒 暴发 的准备,从而实现更有效的早期部署,并有可能减少感染的传播。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是评论性的,没有提供原始数据,这限制了其证据强度。然而,它利用现有的知识和参考资料,对当前 疫苗 准备挑战和机遇进行了高级概述。

analysis_zh.main_results: 主要结果包括观察到肌肉注射疫苗接种仅能不完美地预防呼吸道病毒感染和传播。它还指出,几种用于 COVID-19 的鼻内 疫苗 正在美国和欧洲以外的地区开发或获得许可,但粘膜 疫苗 的准备仍然存在显着差距。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,粘膜 疫苗 可以提供更好的针对呼吸道病毒的保护,特别是如果它们具有明确的免疫学保护相关性并已确定的功效和安全性。这种解释的新颖之处在于它强调了粘膜 疫苗接种 途径在未来大流行防范方面的潜力。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,开发具有已证实的免疫相关性的粘膜 疫苗 可以增强对未来呼吸道病毒 暴发 的准备,从而实现更有效的早期部署,并有可能减少感染的传播。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是评论性的,没有提供原始数据,这限制了其证据强度。然而,它利用现有的知识和参考资料,对当前 疫苗 准备挑战和机遇进行了高级概述。

papers.title: One Health priorities beyond 2026: translating advances in science, surveillance and governance into prevention and preparedness.
papers.abstract: The interdependence of human, animal and environmental health and persistent gaps between multisectoral commitments and effective implementation were highlighted in The Lancet 2023 One Health series. Since then, advances in genomic and environmental surveillance, artificial intelligence and international governance have created new opportunities for infectious disease prevention and preparedness. However, avian influenza A(H5N1), filovirus outbreaks, antimicrobial resistance and the 2026 Andes virus cruise-ship outbreak illustrate continuing challenges in surveillance, coordination and response. Climate-sensitive infections, foodborne zoonoses and environmental contamination further emphasize the need for integrated approaches extending beyond emerging viral threats. This review critically examines developments since 2023, distinguishing established preventive interventions from promising but incompletely validated technologies, and both proximate biosecurity controls and structural socio-ecological upstream prevention, from early detection and outbreak containment. We propose a six-stage surveillance-to-action pathway linking detection, verification, joint risk assessment, accountable decisions, coordinated interventions and double-loop evaluation. An operational matrix illustrates its application across emerging and endemic infections, antimicrobial resistance and environmental threats. Five priorities address interoperable participatory surveillance, evidence-based upstream prevention, integrated antimicrobial resistance action, sustainable national governance that redresses sectoral power asymmetries, and equitable regional capacity. Effective One Health implementation requires clear institutional responsibilities, sustained financing, co-designed community and indigenous participation and rigorous evaluation. Progress should ultimately be measured by demonstrable reductions in infectious disease risks and improved protection of human, animal and environmental health.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the implementation of One Health strategies to address hantaviruses, emphasizing the interdependence of human, animal, and environmental health. It explores the challenges in surveillance, coordination, and response to hantavirus-related diseases, including hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) and hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS). The central question is how to translate scientific and governance advances into effective prevention and preparedness measures for hantaviruses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a critical analysis of developments since the 2023 One Health series, examining both established preventive interventions and emerging technologies. It does not report specific databases, search dates, or study counts, but it highlights the distinction between proximate biosecurity controls and structural socio-ecological prevention strategies. The review also outlines a six-stage surveillance-to-action pathway for integrating these approaches.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that effective One Health implementation is essential for reducing infectious disease risks, particularly for hantaviruses. It emphasizes the need for clear institutional responsibilities, sustained financing, and co-designed community participation. The six-stage surveillance-to-action pathway is proposed as a framework for linking detection, verification, and coordinated interventions.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies gaps in surveillance systems, coordination between sectors, and the validation of new technologies for hantavirus prevention. It also highlights the challenges in addressing climate-sensitive infections and foodborne zoonoses, which require integrated approaches beyond the scope of hantavirus-specific interventions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review proposes five priorities for research and practice: interoperable participatory surveillance, evidence-based upstream prevention, integrated antimicrobial resistance action, sustainable national governance that redresses sectoral power asymmetries, and equitable regional capacity. These priorities aim to improve the prevention and preparedness of hantavirus-related diseases.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the progress and challenges in One Health strategies for hantaviruses since the 2023 Lancet series. It highlights the need for integrated approaches to address surveillance, coordination, and response gaps, particularly in the context of emerging viral threats like the 2026 Andes virus cruise-ship outbreak. The review proposes a six-stage surveillance-to-action pathway and five research and practice priorities to enhance prevention and preparedness. It underscores the importance of clear institutional roles, community participation, and sustainable governance in reducing infectious disease risks, including those associated with hantaviruses.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该审查的重点是实施“同一个健康”战略来解决 汉坦病毒,强调人类、动物和环境健康的相互依赖性。它探讨了 监测、协调和应对汉坦病毒相关疾病的挑战,包括 肾综合征出血热 (HFRS) 和 汉坦病毒肺综合征 (HPS)。核心问题是如何将科学和治理进步转化为有效的汉坦病毒预防和准备措施。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查是对 2023 年“同一个健康”系列以来的发展的批判性分析,审查了既定的预防干预措施和新兴技术。它没有报告具体的数据库、搜索日期或研究计数,但强调了近似生物安全控制和结构性社会生态预防策略之间的区别。该评论还概述了整合这些方法的六阶段 监测 行动路径。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,有效实施“同一个健康”对于降低传染病风险至关重要,特别是对于汉坦病毒而言。它强调需要明确的机构责任、持续的融资和共同设计的社区参与。提出了六阶段 监测 行动路径作为连接检测、验证和协调干预的框架。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查确定了 监测 系统、部门之间的协调以及汉坦病毒预防新技术的验证方面的差距。它还强调了解决气候敏感感染和食源性人畜共患病的挑战,这需要超越汉坦病毒特定干预措施范围的综合方法。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查提出了研究和实践的五个优先事项:可互操作的参与性监测、基于证据的上游预防、综合抗菌素耐药性行动、纠正部门权力不对称的可持续国家治理以及公平的区域能力。这些优先事项旨在改善汉坦病毒相关疾病的预防和准备。

analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查确定了 监测 系统、部门之间的协调以及汉坦病毒预防新技术的验证方面的差距。它还强调了解决气候敏感感染和食源性人畜共患病的挑战,这需要超越汉坦病毒特定干预措施范围的综合方法。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查提出了研究和实践的五个优先事项:可互操作的参与性监测、基于证据的上游预防、综合抗菌素耐药性行动、纠正部门权力不对称的可持续国家治理以及公平的区域能力。这些优先事项旨在改善汉坦病毒相关疾病的预防和准备。

papers.title: Broad-spectrum antiviral database (BSA-DB): a curated collection of broad-spectrum antiviral agents assembled by large language model mining and expert curation
papers.abstract: Viruses included in the World Health Organization R&D Blueprint priority list pose a continuing epidemic and pandemic threat, highlighting the need for rapidly deployable antiviral discovery resources. Broad-spectrum antivirals (BSAs), which are active against multiple viruses, represent promising starting points for pandemic preparedness, yet relevant bioactivity data remain fragmented across public databases. Here we present BSA-DB, a freely accessible resource comprising 13,194 compounds with reported activity ≤ 10000 nM against at least two of 22 Blueprint viruses spanning 10 virus families (initially 23 viruses were selected, but Hantaan virus yielded no compounds meeting this criterion). BSA-DB was obtained from ChEMBL, PubChem and BindingDB, followed by systematic data curation and standardization of viral annotations. Cheminformatic analysis shows that the collection is chemically diverse rather than dominated by a few known antiviral chemotypes, and identifies recurrent scaffolds, structural clusters with broad virus coverage, and promising starting points for antiviral drug discovery. BSA-DB is available at https://bsadb.denovosciences.ai/through an interactive web platform with search, filtering, visualization and bulk-download functionality, and will be continuously expanded with newly available and community-contributed data.

papers.full_text: nature immunology Volume 27 | December 2026 | 2355 | 2355 Vaccinology 2.0 The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the success of vaccine development, but more improvements in vaccine design, equity, manufacturing and changes in public health policy are warranted. O ne of the global health success stories has been the develop­ ment of vaccines. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), we now have vaccines to more than 30 life-threatening infections, which is estimated to prevent 3.5 million to 5 million deaths every year. The recent COVID-19 pandemic showcased vaccine development at its best. Vaccines against SARS-CoV-2 were developed at record speed, facilitated by new technologies such as the mRNA vaccine platform and spurred by the wealth of existing knowledge of virology, vac­ cinology and structural biology. However, much has changed since the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic. In this issue of Nature Immunology, we have commissioned several commentaries from experts across the globe that collectively summarize recent progress and discuss the challenges faced in this field. Although the COVID-19 pandemic high­ lighted the transformative potential of mRNA platforms, gaps remain for global pandemic preparedness according to Florian Kram­ mer. In his Comment, Krammer argues that there is a need to advance mucosal vaccines to improve protection against respiratory infection and transmission, and to develop more broadly protective vaccines that target entire virus families. In addition, strengthen­ ing regulatory policy and sustaining support for basic research on emerging pathogens is needed. However, the current US adminis­ tration has adopted measures that weaken vaccine development in the USA by the deci­ sion to withdraw federal support for mRNA vaccine development. This action led to the cancellation of research grant contracts worth approximately US$500 million, affecting ongoing mRNA therapeutic projects involv­ ing universities, research institutes and major pharmaceutical companies. In addition to funding cuts, the public health policies of the current US government are promoting vaccine hesitancy. In a World View article, Peter Hotez argues that the rise of the US Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) movement has weakened confidence in evidence-based medicine, contributed to out­ breaks of vaccine-preventable diseases such as measles, and fostered efforts to replace established scientific and regulatory frame­ works with wellness-oriented ideologies. Wor­ ryingly, vaccine hesitancy has evolved from a movement focused on COVID-19 vaccines into a broader anti-science campaign that increas­ ingly shapes public health policy, promotes misinformation and extends to areas such as childhood immunization, autism, fluoride, raw milk and alternative medicine. Further­ more, Hotez warns that these trends are spreading internationally, particularly into Europe, raising concerns that growing accept­ ance of pseudoscientific health policies could undermine pandemic preparedness, biomedi­ cal research and public health outcomes on a global scale. On a more optimistic note, in their Com­ ment Michael J. Hogan and Norbert Pardi discuss advances across other RNA technolo­ gies that aim to improve efficacy, reduce reac­ togenicity and enhance T cell and mucosal immune responses. A deeper understanding of RNA and lipid-nanoparticle biology, com­ bined with innovations in delivery systems and immune modulation, is still needed to engi­ neer vaccines that produce different types of immune response depending on the disease being treated. Similarly, the COVID-19 pan­ demic exposed the vulnerability of Africa and other lower-income regions to dependence on external vaccine suppliers. Shabir A. Madhi and Glenda E. Gray state in their Comment that the local manufacturing of routine vaccines in Africa is often economically uncompeti­ tive and may divert resources from broader public health goals. Instead, they advocate for strategic investment in adaptable vaccine platforms such as mRNA and viral-vector technologies, outbreak-response manufac­ turing capacity, regulatory expertise, clini­ cal development infrastructure and skilled workforce development. In their Comment, Rino Rappuoli et al. high­ light the European Vaccines Hub for Pandemic Readiness (EVH) created in response to short­ comings exposed by the COVID-19 pandemic. The EVH is designed to strengthen pandemic preparedness by integrating vaccine and monoclonal antibody discovery, preclinical and clinical development, regulatory plan­ ning and manufacturing capabilities into a coordinated, end-to-end development net­ work. The initiative aims to translate Europe’s strong scientific base into deployable medi­ cal countermeasures for emerging infectious diseases and is currently focusing on threats such as H5N1 influenza. The authors highlight EVH’s early achievements, including the iden­ tification of promising vaccine and antibody candidates, the establishment of clinical trial infrastructure, and rapid responses to emerging threats, such as Andes hantavirus and Ebola Bundibugyo outbreaks. Finally, in his Comment, Bali Pulendran looks at the future of vaccine research by pointing out the vaccine-induced protection extends beyond antibody and T cell responses to encompass a broader spectrum of ‘protec­ tive immune states’ within tissues, in which coordinated networks of immune and non­ immune cells confer heightened resistance to infection. Recent studies of intravenous BCG and mucosal vaccination suggest that protection can emerge from coordinated interactions among adaptive immune cells, innate cells and structural cells within tissues. These interactions create organ-embedded states of increased resistance that provide broad protection against diverse pathogens, a phenomenon termed ‘integrated organ immu­ nity’. Pulendran proposes that future vacci­ nology should shift from focusing primarily on antigens and immune correlates toward identifying, characterizing and deliberately engineering these protective immune states, potentially enabling more durable and broadly protective vaccines against infectious diseases and other immune-mediated conditions. This ‘Vaccinology 2.0’ focus highlights the achievements of vaccine research in the past 6 years and showcases issues that still need to be tackled to ensure the continued development, improvement and accessibility of vaccines for future generations and ensure that we are prepared for the next pandemic. Published online: 23 November 2026 Editorial https://doi.org/10.1038/s41590-026-02725-x Check for updates

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need for improvements in vaccine design, equity, manufacturing and public health policy, particularly in the context of global pandemic preparedness and the challenges faced in the field of vaccinology.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is an editorial in Nature Immunology, published in December 2026, which compiles commentaries from experts on recent progress and challenges in vaccinology, focusing on the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent policy changes.
analysis.methods: The editorial summarizes expert commentaries and discusses the development of vaccines, including mRNA platforms, and the challenges in vaccine development, such as funding cuts and public health policy shifts.
analysis.main_results: The editorial reports that vaccines have been developed for over 30 life-threatening infections, preventing an estimated 3.5 million to 5 million deaths annually. It also highlights the rapid development of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines and the challenges in global pandemic preparedness.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that while the pandemic showcased the potential of mRNA vaccines, significant gaps remain in global preparedness. They emphasize the need for advancements in mucosal vaccines and regulatory frameworks to address these challenges.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of advancing mucosal vaccines and strengthening regulatory policies to improve pandemic preparedness and public health outcomes globally.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on an editorial and expert commentaries, which may be subject to bias and lack rigorous statistical analysis. The confidence in the findings is moderate due to the nature of the source.

analysis.summary_en: The editorial 'Vaccinology 2.0' in Nature Immunology, published in December 2026, discusses the successes and challenges in vaccine development, particularly in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic. It highlights the rapid development of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines using new technologies like mRNA platforms, but also points out gaps in global pandemic preparedness. The editorial emphasizes the need for advancements in mucosal vaccines to improve protection against respiratory infections and transmission, as well as the importance of regulatory policy and sustained support for basic research on emerging pathogens. It also notes the impact of the US Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) movement on vaccine confidence and public health policy. While the editorial provides a broad overview of the field, it lacks detailed statistical analysis and is based on expert commentaries, which may introduce bias. The findings suggest that improving vaccine design and public health policies is crucial for future pandemic preparedness and global health outcomes.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了改进 疫苗 设计、公平、制造和公共卫生政策的需要,特别是在全球大流行防范和疫苗学领域面临的挑战的背景下。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是《自然免疫学》杂志上的一篇社论,于 2026 年 12 月发表,其中汇集了专家对疫苗学最新进展和挑战的评论,重点关注了 COVID-19 大流行的影响以及随后的政策变化。
elements_zh.methods: 该社论总结了专家评论,并讨论了 疫苗 的发展,包括 mRNA 平台,以及 疫苗 发展中面临的挑战,例如资金削减和公共卫生政策转变。
elements_zh.main_results: The editorial reports that vaccines have been developed for over 30 life-threatening infections, preventing an estimated 3.5 million to 5 million deaths annually. It also highlights the rapid development of SARS-CoV-2 vaccines and the challenges in global pandemic preparedness.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,虽然这次大流行展示了 mRNA 疫苗 的潜力,但全球准备工作仍存在重大差距。他们强调需要改进粘膜 疫苗 和监管框架来应对这些挑战。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明了推进粘膜 疫苗 和加强监管政策以改善全球大流行防范和公共卫生结果的重要性。

papers.full_text: nature immunology Volume 27 | December 2026 | 2363–2365 | 2363 The European Vaccines Hub Rino Rappuoli, Isabelle Bekeredjian-Ding, Pierre Van Damme, James P. Di Santo, Donata Medaglini & Michel Pletschette The European Vaccines Hub is a novel design consortium that assembles leading European organizations involved in vaccine development. The mission is to develop vaccines and monoclonal antibodies ensuring Europe’s pandemics and emerging infections readiness. When the COVID-19 pandemic struck the European Union, it was insufficiently prepared to face the devastating health and economic emergency. Although European biotech contributed significantly to the development of vaccines with products such as Comirnaty, the mRNA vaccine developed by the German BioNTech was eventually licensed to and commercialized by an American company, meaning that very few European medical countermeasures reached the market at the peak of the pandemic. A further weakness identified was that Europe did not partici- pate in any of the pivotal efficacy trials leading to licensure. To address this situation, the European Commission established the Health Emergency Preparedness and Response Authority (HERA) as one of its Directorates General, with the mission of strengthening the European Union’s ability to respond to major health threats through coordination, expertise and the development and procurement of medical countermeasures (MCMs). In the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic, HERA published a call for proposals for the creation of a European Hub for vaccine development, with the mission of developing, assessing and manufacturing vaccines for priority pathogens with epidemic and pandemic potential to ensure that Europe would be more resilient through increased preparedness. This new entity was designed to be not another institution, but rather a newly created network of existing organizations already funded by their member states to develop vaccines. The mandate of the European Vaccines Hub for Pandemic Readiness (EVH) was to create a hub able to develop and deliver vaccines end-to-end, from discovery to manufacturing. To achieve this, the EVH was expected to be organ- ized in an agile manner, allowing it to make quick decisions and to include and engage with any group from industry, biotech or academia that could contribute to development of vaccines and monoclonal antibodies against pathogens with pandemic risk. Unique new structure The EVH consortium selected for funding enabled the creation of an innovative organization that has the expertise and facilities to provide the European Union with self-sustainable and independent ability to discover, develop, assess and manufacture vaccines and antibodies against infectious diseases of epidemic and pandemic potential. This organization is based on four pillars (Fig. 1). Pillar 1 leads vaccines and monoclonal antibody discovery while advancing platforms to develop vaccines based on protein and adjuvants, on mRNA or on viral vectors. Pillar 2 drives preclinical studies to support the discovery, charac- terization and development of vaccines and monoclonal antibodies. Pillar 3 coordinates clinical development, which includes the readiness to perform ad hoc phase 1 and 2 studies and controlled human challenge studies (CHIM), with the overarching goals of putting together a network of European vaccine clinical trial centers under consented protocols and preparing to conduct large-scale phase 3 studies in collaboration with the EU ‘BE READY NOW’ project. In pillar 4, the German Center for Infection Research (DZIF) and the Center for Pandemic Vaccines and Therapeutics (ZEPAI) oversee regulatory coordination and planning of manufacturing of small-scale Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) lots for early clinical studies, as well as large-scale manufacturing of final products. Although the primary scope of the EVH is to develop and build the capacity to deliver medical countermeasures, it is designed as an open organization that reaches out and engages with small and large vaccine manufacturers, biotech, academic groups, R&D units of pharmaceuti- cal companies, and projects and networks funded by European Union, for example through the Horizon Europe program. To achieve this, the EVH is following two noteworthy paths: the creation of an innovative public–private partnership model with industry and the promotion of ‘expression of interest’ calls for experts and specific projects, enabling the EVH to liaise with experts and collaborating centers that share a similar mission, both within and outside the European Union. The arrows below each pillar in Fig. 1 denote the continuous interchange between the EVH and the European system.
