The initial priority pathogens identified were avian influ- enza, in particular H5N1, and monkeypox (mpox). EVH activities include building the preparedness system and testing it. Indeed, the EVH’s mission creates a system that allows continuous delivery and regular updates for priorities. A living EU Epidemic and Pandemic Vaccine Readiness Plan agreed to with HERA generates an agile basis for EU pandemic preparedness. One year after the EVH was established, each of the four pillars has initiated a variety of projects and delivered important results. Pillar 1 discovered a potent and broadly protective monoclonal anti- body against mpox that recognizes a vaccine antigen not previously known to induce neutralizing antibodies. In vivo and in vitro studies in collaboration with pillar 2 confirmed that the mpox monoclonal antibody and the vaccine antigen are protective in vivo and are good candidates for continued MCM development. Pillar 3 has designed and fully enrolled a clinical trial to study the vaccine response of the European population to primary and booster immunization against the avian influenza H5N1, and is currently assessing its outcome. In the trial, H5N1-naive participants and participants immunized in 2006 with a H5N1 vaccine received an adjuvanted vaccine against the current Astrakhan clade. The study has the additional scope to establish a study cohort whose peripheral blood cells can be used to discover broadly neutralizing antibodies that recognize epitopes shared between the 2006 and 2026 H5N1 strains. Pillar 4 is addressing important bottlenecks in preparedness by mapping the European GMP facilities ready to manufacture vaccines and monoclonals for small-scale clinical trials and developing concepts for rapid ramp-up to large-scale manufacturing in pandemic crises. Its regulatory experts are addressing the anticipated practical and scientific regulatory questions required for accelerating development of EVH products to enable early availability of products. In addition, the EVH has initiated collaborations with external entities. One involves joint participation with Sanofi, a major Euro- pean vaccine manufacturer, in an EU tender to develop a mucosal mRNA vaccine against the H5N1 avian influenza. Another involves the publication of an ‘expression of interest’ to identify possible col- laborators that can contribute to further pandemic influenza vaccine development approaches. Stress testing While the EVH was working on setting up its organization, two unex- pected, highly lethal emerging infections were communicated by the World Health Organization in May 2026. The first was the Andes hanta- virus outbreak, reported on 2 May, involving a cruise ship coming out of Argentina1, and the second was the Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda that was declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 17 May2. Although these were not imminent threats for Europe, after rapid consultation with HERA, it was agreed that it would be important for Europe to par- ticipate in the development of countermeasures for these viruses. The question was whether the EVH had the capacity to address these two targets that, up to that moment, had never been considered. Consultation of the EVH network identified a broadly protective human monoclonal antibody against Andes hantavirus discovered in a Swedish patient infected with Puumala hantavirus, which had been characterized by several German academic groups and whose structure had been determined a few years ago at the Institut Pasteur in Paris3. This antibody had been acquired and improved by two US R&D enterprises but was never brought into clinical development. Concurrently, the German Center for Infection Research (DZIF) labora- tories revealed recent results identifying a potent human monoclonal antibody that neutralizes both Ebola Zaire and Ebola Bundibugyo. The antibody had been shown to protect mice from challenge with the virus in the Biosafety Level 4 (BSL4) facility in Marburg4. As such, in less than a month, the two antibodies were selected by the EVH for development up to clinical testing. For antibody expression, EVH is developing an innovative platform based on the C1 fungus, which is expected to enable cost-effective production of large quantities of monoclonal antibodies, making these therapies more accessible to at-risk populations and to low-income countries at an affordable and equitable cost5. The stress test arising from the unexpected outbreaks showed that the EVH can leverage the ad hoc development of a multitude of innova- tive prototypes from excellent European entities that have hitherto failed to translate them into products when working in isolation. The EVH can turn these product candidates into countermeasures to protect people’s health. Moreover, the EVH network had at its disposal two vac- cine prototypes for the development of an Ebola vaccine: an MVA-based vaccine against Ebola Zaire developed by DZIF-associated EVH mem- bers, previously shown to be protective in a mouse challenge study performed at the Marburg BSL-4 facility6, and a measles vector-based pan-filovirus vaccine in development at the Institut Pasteur. Once added to the EVH portfolio, these projects could become highly relevant in the race against Bundibugyo virus. Furthermore, monoclonal antibodies candidates could provide an important complementary strategy, with the advantage of providing immediate protection. Looking to the future In conclusion, the EVH is an organization rooting pandemic prepar- edness within an innovative cross-sectorial ecosystem, which in its first year of existence has shown the potential to deliver innovative countermeasures. We can probably describe the EVH as both a dis- covery and development engine and a catalyst able to aggregate the best European competencies and discoveries, transforming them into medical products that include vaccines and monoclonal antibodies. The big question is whether the EVH will be able to exploit this poten- tial and deliver real products. There are numerous challenges that could interfere with this ambitious goal. One of the most important limitations is the fact that the products in the EVH portfolio do not have an immediate attractive commercial market value because they address infectious diseases that are rare, or pandemics that we hope will never happen. The absence of immediate commercial value, com- monly defined as a market failure, is a recurrent problem for most medical countermeasures. In the absence of an expected immediate and secure return on investment, the private sector is little inclined to start rapid development and manufacturing programs. Notwithstand- ing that complication, the instruments developed by the EU in terms of stockpiling essential and possibly innovative MCMs and the constant readiness of the reality-tested joint procurement mechanism are robust attempts to provide solutions to these problems. Although we have the technology to develop effective products against most infectious diseases, these need to become available for wide implementation despite the absence of immediate pre- dictable markets. It is therefore important to address, on a global scale, the longer-term sustainability of MCM development, which can be clearly seen to be an insurance for the health and economic security of every country, and to move out of the disastrous cycle of panic and neglect. nature immunology Volume 27 | December 2026 | 2363–2365 | 2365 Comment Rino Rappuoli 1,2 , Isabelle Bekeredjian-Ding1,3,4, Pierre Van Damme 1,5, James P. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the European Union’s lack of preparedness for pandemics and emerging infections, particularly highlighting the insufficiency of its capacity to develop and deliver medical countermeasures during the COVID-19 pandemic.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study describes the establishment of the European Vaccines Hub (EVH) as a consortium of existing European organizations, designed to enhance pandemic readiness through coordinated vaccine development and manufacturing efforts.
analysis.methods: The EVH was structured as a network of organizations already funded by member states, with a focus on agile decision-making and collaboration with industry, biotech, and academic groups to develop vaccines and monoclonal antibodies against priority pathogens.
analysis.main_results: HERA published a call for proposals to create the EVH, which was designed to develop and deliver vaccines end-to-end, from discovery to manufacturing, ensuring increased preparedness for future health threats.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the creation of the EVH as a novel approach to strengthen Europe’s ability to respond to pandemics, emphasizing its role in fostering collaboration and rapid decision-making.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the EVH can enhance Europe’s capacity to develop and deploy medical countermeasures against epidemic and pandemic pathogens, thereby improving public health preparedness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study does not report specific limitations, but it is based on a general description of the EVH’s design and mission, which may not fully account for potential challenges in implementation.

analysis.summary_en: This study highlights the need for improved pandemic preparedness in the European Union, particularly in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, where Europe lacked sufficient capacity to develop and deliver medical countermeasures. The European Vaccines Hub (EVH) was established as a consortium of existing organizations to enhance readiness through coordinated vaccine development and manufacturing. The EVH is designed to be an agile network that engages with various stakeholders, including industry, biotech, and academia, to develop vaccines and monoclonal antibodies against pathogens with pandemic potential. The authors interpret the EVH as a novel approach to strengthen Europe’s response capabilities, emphasizing its role in fostering collaboration and rapid decision-making. The findings suggest that the EVH can improve the EU’s capacity to respond to future health threats, contributing to public health preparedness. The evidence is general in nature, describing the mission and structure of the EVH, and does not include detailed limitations or specific results.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决欧盟对流行病和新出现的感染缺乏准备的问题,特别强调其在 COVID-19 大流行期间制定和提供医疗对策的能力不足。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究描述了欧洲 疫苗 中心 (EVH) 的建立,作为现有欧洲组织的联盟,旨在通过协调 疫苗 开发和制造工作来加强大流行准备工作。
analysis_zh.methods: EVH 的结构是一个由成员国资助的组织网络,重点是敏捷决策以及与工业、生物技术和学术团体的合作,开发 疫苗 和针对优先病原体的单克隆抗体。
analysis_zh.main_results: HERA 发布了创建 EVH 的提案征集,该 EVH 旨在开发和提供从发现到制造的端到端 疫苗,确保加强对未来健康威胁的准备。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将 EVH 的创建解释为增强欧洲应对流行病能力的一种新方法,强调其在促进合作和快速决策方面的作用。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,EVH 可以增强欧洲针对流行病和大流行病原体制定和部署医疗对策的能力,从而改善公共卫生准备。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究没有报告具体的局限性,但它是基于对 EVH 设计和使命的一般描述,这可能无法充分考虑实施中的潜在挑战。

OffOn Stream on 3 dead in suspected hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship: What to know The ship is off the coast of Cape Verde with 149 people on board. ByMary Kekatos May 4, 2026, 11:34 PM A rare rodent-borne disease may be behind a deadly outbreak aboard a cruise ship. There have been two laboratory-confirmed cases and five suspected cases of hantavirus, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Of those seven people, three have died between April 11 and May 2 and one is currently in intensive care, according to the WHO. The WHO said Monday that investigations into the deaths and illnesses are ongoing, including further laboratory testing. Related The tragic deaths of Gene Hackman and Betsy Arakawa: A timeline The outbreak was reported on the MV Hondius, run by Oceanwide Expeditions, which was traveling between Argentina and the Canary Islands via Cape Verde. Currently, the ship is off the coast of Cape Verde with 149 people on board representing 23 different nationalities, Oceanwide Expeditions said in a press release on Monday. Here's what you need to know about the outbreak, what hantavirus is and how it spreads. This aerial picture shows a general view of the cruise ship MV Hondius stationary off the port of Praia, the capital of Cape Verde, on May 4, 2026. AFP via Getty Images Timeline of the outbreak South African health officials said in a statement on Monday that the first two deaths occurred in a married couple from the Netherlands. The 70-year-old male passenger became ill first with a fever, headache, abdominal pain and diarrhea starting on April 6. He passed away on board on April 11, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. No microbiological test were performed, according to the WHO. The deceased passenger's wife, 69, went ashore at St. Helena, a British territory in the South Atlantic Ocean, on April 24 with gastrointestinal symptoms, according to health officials. She collapsed at Johannesburg O.R. Tambo International Airport while trying to connect to fly home to the Netherlands on April 25, and was taken to a medical facility in nearby Kempton Park, according to health officials. She passed away on April 26, and her laboratory test results have come back positive for hantavirus, according to the WHO. Another patient, a British national, fell ill while the ship was traveling from St. Helena to Ascension, also a British territory, according to the South African health officials' statement. The passenger began showing symptoms on April 24 and he was medically evacuated from Ascension to South Africa on April 27, according to the WHO. "Despite medical treatment provided to him at Ascension, his condition did not improve and necessitated his medical evacuation to a South African private health facility in Sandton for further medical management," South African health officials said. The patient is currently in critical condition in isolation but receiving medical attention, according to health officials, who said his laboratory test results came back positive for hantavirus. A fourth passenger presented with pneumonia symptoms starting on April 28, according to the WHO. The German woman died on May 2 from causes not yet known, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. Related These US cities could see surge in disease-spreading pests this spring Meanwhile, there are three symptomatic people who remain on board the MV Hondius with suspected hantavirus cases, according to the WHO. Two crew members -- one of British nationality and one of Dutch nationality -- have acute respiratory symptoms. One has a mild illness and the other severe symptoms, with both requiring urgent medical care, Oceanwide Expeditions said. A third person also remains on board reporting high fever and/or gastrointestinal symptoms, according to the WHO. No other people with symptoms have been identified, Oceanwide Expeditions said Monday. Guests will not be disembarking in Cape Verde, expect for the three people who will be medically evacuated, according to Oceanwide Expeditions. "At this stage, a definitive disembarkation point for the remaining guests on board m/v Hondius has not been finalized," the company said Monday. "Sailing on to Las Palmas or Tenerife is being considered, where further medical screening and handling could take place, organized and supervised by the WHO and Dutch health services." The logo of shipping company Oceanwide Expeditions, which operates MV Hondius cruise ship, in Vlissingen, The Netherlands, May 4, 2026. Provicom/EPA/Shutterstock "Strict precautionary measures are in process on board, including isolation measures, hygiene protocols and medical monitoring. All passengers have been informed and are being supported," the company said. "We understand the considerable interest and concern and will share new information as soon as it has been verified." "WHO is facilitating medical evacuation of two symptomatic passengers, conducting a full risk assessment, and supporting affected people onboard," Ghebreysus wrote. What is hantavirus? Hantaviruses are a family of viruses that can cause serious illnesses and death, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The viruses cause two syndromes: hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). HPS is mostly found in the Western Hemisphere, including the U.S., and HFRS is mostly found in Europe and Asia. Stock photo of a colorized electron micrograph of the Hantavirus. Alfred Pasieka/Science Photo Lib/STOCK PHOTO/Getty Images Surveillance for hantavirus in the U.S. began in 1993 during an outbreak in the Four Corners region, where Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and Utah meet, the CDC said. Between 1993 and the end of 2023, 890 cases of hantavirus disease have been reported in the U.S., according to the CDC. Hantavirus became more widely known after being identified as the cause of death of the wife of actor Gene Hackman after the couple was found dead at their New Mexico home in February 2025. How does hantavirus spread? Hantaviruses are usually spread through rodents, including rats and mice, mostly from exposure to urine, droppings or saliva. Although the viruses can spread through a rodent bite or scratch, such infection is rare, the CDC says. Hantaviruses may also spread from person to person but that also is rare and only suspected for one subtype from South America, according to the WHO. What are the hantavirus symptoms? HPS symptoms typically appear from one to eight weeks after contact with the virus, with early signs including fever, fatigue and muscle aches, according to the CDC. Half of HPS patients will experience headaches, chills, dizziness, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and abdominal pain. The CDC says that between four and 10 days after the initial phase of illness, the late symptoms will appear, including coughing, shortness of breath and tightness in the chest as the lungs fill with fluid. Related Gene Hackman's wife died of hantavirus; actor died of cardiovascular disease, Alzheimer's: Officials About 38% of people who develop HPS respiratory symptoms may die from the disease, according to the CDC. Symptoms of HFRS usually develop one to two weeks after exposure and typically include intense headaches, fever, chills, back pain, abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting, the CDC says. Later symptoms may include low blood pressure, lack of blood flow, internal bleeding and acute kidney failure. Depending on the virus causing the infection, fatality among infected humans can range from less than 1% to as high as 15%, the CDC says. What hantavirus treatments are available? No specific treatment is available for hantavirus infection, with the CDC recommending patients receive supportive care such as rest, hydration and treatment of symptoms. Because HPS can cause breathing difficulties, patients may need breathing support, such as intubation, the CDC says. Because HFRS can disrupt kidney function, infected patients may need dialysis to remove toxins from the blood, according to the CDC. news.content: 🦠 Hantavirus: how did the virus spread during the cruise? Techno-Science News▼ Technologies Aeronautics Transportation Space Energy Digital Architecture Sciences Mathematics Physics Astrophysics Astronomy Life and Earth Archaeology Others Other Subjects Forum▼ Technologies Aeronautics Transportation Space Energy Digital Architecture Sciences Mathematics Physics Astrophysics Astronomy Life and Earth Archaeology Others Other Subjects Discussions Current Events & Society Culture Classifieds Chit-Chat 🦠 Hantavirus: how did the virus spread during the cruise? Several months after the hantavirus outbreak that affected passengers on the Hondius, scientists have a better understanding of how the virus spread on board. On April 1, 2026, the cruise ship left Ushuaia, in southern Argentina. Two days later, a passenger developed the first symptoms of the disease. They died on April 11. Others fell ill afterward, sometimes several weeks after leaving the ship. In total, the outbreak caused three deaths among 13 reported cases. The cruise ship Hondius, seen from the front and slightly to one side, in Magdalenefjord, Svalbard, on June 24, 2025. Photo: Stefan Brending, 2025 Hondius - IMO 9818709 by 2eight - 9SC5017, CC BY-SA 3.0 DE. Hantaviruses usually circulate among certain wild rodents. People can become infected by breathing in dust contaminated with the animals’ urine or droppings. However, the Andes virus, identified in patients from the Hondius, has a distinctive feature: it can also spread between people. A key question arises: were passengers infected separately by rodents, or did one passenger bring the virus on board? An international team, including researchers from the Institut Pasteur and the University of Geneva, compared when symptoms began. One late case caught their attention in particular: symptoms appeared 60 days after departure from Argentina. According to available data, symptoms appear no later than six weeks after infection from a rodent. That period had therefore been exceeded. The researchers established, however, that this patient had been in close, prolonged contact with another sick passenger. These findings strengthen the hypothesis of human-to-human transmission. The scientists also analyzed the virus’s genetic material from samples taken from ten patients. When a virus multiplies, small changes can occur in its genome. Studying these changes can sometimes help trace chains of infection. The viruses found in the patients were almost identical. The results therefore point to a single introduction of the virus on board, followed by successive human-to-human transmissions. Has the virus become more contagious? The researchers found no known mutations that would promote its transmission between people. The observed infections remain consistent with close, prolonged contact. A second study found that the Hondius virus was closely related to the one responsible for an outbreak in Argentina in 2018. Viruses from this same lineage were still circulating in northern Patagonia in 2025. The World Health Organization declared the outbreak over on July 2, 2026, after monitoring more than 650 people who may have been exposed to the virus. 0/500 Minimum: 2 BA Barque Lai 19 hours ago Why didn't this or these famous singers in France report it after their stays in Patagonia? Rodents are not picky, they also love any music or song... 1 View comments Follow us on Google

analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 暴发 导致 13 例报告病例中 3 人死亡。该病毒被确定为安第斯病毒,已知会在人与人之间传播。观察到的感染与密切、长时间的接触一致,并且没有发现突变会增加其传播性。
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 在监测了 650 多名潜在暴露者后,世界卫生组织于 2026 年 7 月 2 日宣布 暴发 结束。该调查包括对 10 名患者的病毒进行基因分析,这支持了人传人 传播 的假设。不过,船上病毒的确切来源仍在调查中。

news.wechat_summary_zh: 时间：暴发 事件于 2026 年 4 月报告，第一个症状出现在游轮于 2026 年 4 月 1 日离开阿根廷乌斯怀亚两天后。最后一个病...；地点与对象：洪迪斯号游轮从阿根廷南部的乌斯怀亚出发，随后前往斯瓦尔巴群岛马格达莱讷峡湾。受影响的人群包括船上的乘客，已报告病例 13 例，死亡 3 例。；事件：Hondius 号游轮上发生了一次 暴发 的 汉坦病毒，有证据表明存在人传人的 传播。科学家对暴发进行了分析，发现该病毒很可能是在船上传播的，并通过密切、长时间的接触在乘客之间传播。；影响与风险：暴发 导致 13 例报告病例中 3 人死亡。该病毒被确定为安第斯病毒，已知会在人与人之间传播。观察到的感染与密切、长时间的接触一致，并且没有发现突变会增加其传播性。；应对与不确定性：在监测了 650 多名潜在暴露者后，世界卫生组织于 2026 年 7 月 2 日宣布 暴发 结束。该调查包括对 10 名患者的病毒进行基因分析，这支持了人传人 传播 的假设。不过，船上病毒的确切来源仍在调查中。

news.content: World Society Russia Opinion Science Sport Incidents Animal Russia World Society Science Incidents Opinion Business News All > 08:19 Maldives E-Gates: Which 30 Airlines Allow Skip-the-Line Passport Control 07:39 AFT Pharmaceutical posts $6.9m half-year profit as revenue crosses $143m for the first time 07:38 Fisher & Paykel Healthcare lifts full-year profit guidance after 37 percent half-year net profit surge 07:17 World Rugby suspends Oceania Rugby council seat pending governance inquiry 06:56 New Cook Strait ferries to cut emissions by 30 percent from 2029 06:46 Meridian Energy secures minority stake in Datagrid's Southland AI data centre 06:26 Why Liquid Oil Worsens Stiff Locks and the Safer Pencil Alternative 05:56 Why Warm Water and Dish Soap Clear Minor Toilet Clogs Without Damage 05:35 Chrome Oxidation: When Aluminum Foil Works and When It Fails Hantavirus infection symptoms: how to distinguish early HFRS from common seasonal influenza 26.11.2026 08:04 Health Every spring, a wave of anxiety ripples through certain communities regarding a condition often colloquially called "mouse fever." The clinical name-Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS)-sounds far more daunting than a common cold, and because many general practitioners may never encounter a case in their entire career, the fear is often driven by the unknown rather than the actual statistical risk. Photo: Pravda.Ru by ÐÐ1⁄4Ð ̧ÑÑÐ ̧Ð1 ÐÐμÐ»Ð3⁄4Ð2 is licensed under ÐÑÐμ Ð¿ÑÐ°Ð2Ð° Ð·Ð°ÑÐ ̧ÑÐμÐ1⁄2Ñ Measuring a manâs temperature Understanding the Risk Profile Objectively, HFRS is not a mass epidemic. In Russia, annual cases typically range between 3,400 and 7,000. However, the geography of the risk is highly concentrated; approximately 80% of cases are centered in the Volga region. In contrast, the Moscow region sees only sporadic instances, averaging between 5 and 17 people per year. Data from Rospotrebnadzor in 2026 indicated that the epidemiological situation remains stable and controlled, with no major outbreaks, though localized activity persists in areas like Tatarstan and the Altai Territory, where most cases recently reported followed a mild course. The Anatomy of a Symptom The term "hemorrhagic" refers to a tendency toward bleeding. In typical cases, this manifests as petechiae-tiny, pinpoint hemorrhages under the skin-or red spots on the whites of the eyes. More concerning are internal bleedings, such as hematuria (blood in the urine), which indicates that the kidneys are under stress. Renal failure is the primary complication of HFRS and can develop rapidly, sometimes requiring hemodialysis (an "artificial kidney" machine) to clear the blood. The "fever" aspect of the disease is also distinct from the flu. While both begin with a sharp rise in temperature (38.5-40°C), accompanied by chills, muscle aches, and a severe headache, HFRS has a telling characteristic: the lack of relief after the fever drops. While a flu-like illness often peaks and subsides, the febrile period of HFRS typically lasts five to seven days, often followed by a phase where kidney impairment becomes apparent. Because the early signs mimic a common respiratory infection, patients may mistake the illness for a cold and delay seeking a professional diagnosis. How Transmission Actually Happens HFRS is a focal infection, meaning it is tied to specific environments. In European Russia, the Puumala hantavirus, carried by the bank vole, is responsible for 90-95% of infections. These rodents do not fall ill themselves but shed the virus through saliva, urine, and feces throughout their lives. They frequent areas near human habitation, including forests, summer cottages, garages, and basements. The primary route of infection is airborne. When dried rodent excretions are disturbed-during the cleaning of a dusty garage, handling hay, or changing tires-the virus becomes aerosolized as dust. When a person inhales this dust, the virus enters the lungs. Less common routes include contact through broken skin or the consumption of contaminated food. Recovery and Long-term Outlook The prognosis depends heavily on the virus strain and the speed of diagnosis. In European Russia, where the milder Puumala strain circulates, the fatality rate is low, ranging from 0.3% to 2%. However, in the Far East, more aggressive serotypes (Hantaan and Amur) can lead to fatality rates between 5% and 10%. Recovery is a gradual process. While hospital discharge usually occurs after two to three weeks, full rehabilitation can take several months. Patients often report lingering weakness, fatigue, and fluctuations in blood pressure. While the majority of people regain full kidney and vascular function, some may develop chronic kidney disease or associated hypertension. Crucially, HFRS is not transmitted from person to person; it is strictly a rodent-to-human transmission. If you experience an acute fever, severe headache, and muscle pain-particularly after spending time in enclosed spaces where rodents may have been present-it is essential to avoid self-medication. The clinical name-Hemorrhagic Fever with Renal Syndrome (HFRS)-sounds far more daunting than a common cold, and because many general practitioners may never encounter a case in their entire career, the fear is often driven by the unknown rather than the actual statistical risk. Photo: Pravda.Ru by ÐÐ1⁄4Ð ̧ÑÑÐ ̧Ð1 ÐÐμÐ»Ð3⁄4Ð2 is licensed under ÐÑÐμ Ð¿ÑÐ°Ð2Ð° Ð·Ð°ÑÐ ̧ÑÐμÐ1⁄2Ñ Measuring a manâs temperature Understanding the Risk Profile Objectively, HFRS is not a mass epidemic. In Russia, annual cases typically range between 3,400 and 7,000. However, the geography of the risk is highly concentrated; approximately 80% of cases are centered in the Volga region. In contrast, the Moscow region sees only sporadic instances, averaging between 5 and 17 people per year. Data from Rospotrebnadzor in 2026 indicated that the epidemiological situation remains stable and controlled, with no major outbreaks, though localized activity persists in areas like Tatarstan and the Altai Territory, where most cases recently reported followed a mild course. The Anatomy of a Symptom The term "hemorrhagic" refers to a tendency toward bleeding. In typical cases, this manifests as petechiae-tiny, pinpoint hemorrhages under the skin-or red spots on the whites of the eyes. More concerning are internal bleedings, such as hematuria (blood in the urine), which indicates that the kidneys are under stress. Renal failure is the primary complication of HFRS and can develop rapidly, sometimes requiring hemodialysis (an "artificial kidney" machine) to clear the blood. The "fever" aspect of the disease is also distinct from the flu. While both begin with a sharp rise in temperature (38.5-40°C), accompanied by chills, muscle aches, and a severe headache, HFRS has a telling characteristic: the lack of relief after the fever drops. While a flu-like illness often peaks and subsides, the febrile period of HFRS typically lasts five to seven days, often followed by a phase where kidney impairment becomes apparent. Because the early signs mimic a common respiratory infection, patients may mistake the illness for a cold and delay seeking a professional diagnosis. How Transmission Actually Happens HFRS is a focal infection, meaning it is tied to specific environments. In European Russia, the Puumala hantavirus, carried by the bank vole, is responsible for 90-95% of infections. These rodents do not fall ill themselves but shed the virus through saliva, urine, and feces throughout their lives. They frequent areas near human habitation, including forests, summer cottages, garages, and basements. The primary route of infection is airborne. When dried rodent excretions are disturbed-during the cleaning of a dusty garage, handling hay, or changing tires-the virus becomes aerosolized as dust. When a person inhales this dust, the virus enters the lungs. Less common routes include contact through broken skin or the consumption of contaminated food. Recovery and Long-term Outlook The prognosis depends heavily on the virus strain and the speed of diagnosis. In European Russia, where the milder Puumala strain circulates, the fatality rate is low, ranging from 0.3% to 2%. However, in the Far East, more aggressive serotypes (Hantaan and Amur) can lead to fatality rates between 5% and 10%. Recovery is a gradual process. While hospital discharge usually occurs after two to three weeks, full rehabilitation can take several months. Patients often report lingering weakness, fatigue, and fluctuations in blood pressure. While the majority of people regain full kidney and vascular function, some may develop chronic kidney disease or associated hypertension. Crucially, HFRS is not transmitted from person to person; it is strictly a rodent-to-human transmission. If you experience an acute fever, severe headache, and muscle pain-particularly after spending time in enclosed spaces where rodents may have been present-it is essential to avoid self-medication. Please consult a healthcare provider to determine the cause of your symptoms and ensure the appropriate course of action is taken. news.content_zh: 本文于26.11.2026发表,讨论了汉坦病毒感染的症状,特别是肾综合征出血热(肾综合征出血热),并强调了将其与常见季节性流感区分开来的重要性。肾综合征出血热不是大规模流行病,俄罗斯每年的病例数通常在3,400至7,000例之间。大多数病例集中在伏尔加地区,而莫斯科地区仅见零星病例,每年平均5-17例。文章指出,肾综合征出血热不会在人与人之间传播,而是严格通过啮齿动物传播。死亡率因病毒株而异,欧洲俄罗斯较温和的普乌玛拉株死亡率较低(0.3-2%),而远东地区更具攻击性的汉坦病毒和阿穆尔病毒株则导致较高的死亡率(5-10%)。流行病学情况保持稳定和可控,没有报告重大暴发,尽管在塔塔尔斯坦和阿尔泰地区等地方仍存在局部活动,且病例病情较轻。文章强调,肾综合征出血热的早期症状可能与流感相似,可能导致诊断的延误。

analysis.event: A suspected case of hantavirus was identified in Portugal, but the test result was negative. The Directorate-General of Health (DGS) confirmed the patient's symptoms were not related to hantavirus.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: No cases, deaths, or exposures were reported. The risk level was not explicitly stated, but the case was ruled out as hantavirus.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The case was tested and ruled out as hantavirus. The patient was referred back to Curry Cabral Hospital. The investigation is complete, and no further action is required.

analysis.brief_en: A suspected case of hantavirus in Portugal was reported on 18 May 2026, when a patient was admitted to São Francisco Xavier Hospital with symptoms that raised concerns. However, the test conducted on the patient, as reported by Lusa and cited by Observador, came back negative, and she was subsequently referred back to Curry Cabral Hospital. The Directorate-General of Health (DGS) confirmed that the symptoms were not related to hantavirus. The article was published on 23 November 2026 by The Portugal News, and no further details on the case or its implications were provided. The case was resolved as not being hantavirus, and no additional actions or risk assessments were mentioned in the evidence. The report does not indicate any broader outbreak or public health response related to hantavirus in Portugal.

news.content_title: Decoding the origins of the Hanta virus on the Argentinian cruise ship.
news.content: Decoding the origins of the Hanta virus on the Argentinian cruise ship. Two new international studies published in the journal Science have shed light on the transmission pathways and evolutionary history of the Andean Hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius cruise ship in April of this year. Check Symptoms VietnamPlus • 24/11/2026 According to the Vietnam News Agency correspondent in Argentina, two new international studies published in the journal Science have shed light on the transmission pathways and evolutionary history of the Andean Hantavirus outbreak on the MV Hondius cruise ship in April of this year. The results confirmed that the virus was transmitted from person to person at sea, and traced its genetic profile back to a strain of virus that had circulated in northern Patagonia (Argentina) many years prior. The outbreak occurred after the MV Hondius departed from Ushuaia, Argentina, on April 1st to cross the South Atlantic. A total of 13 passengers and crew members developed severe respiratory illness (12 confirmed cases and 1 suspected case), resulting in 3 deaths. Tests identified the causative agent as an Andes virus – a type of Hanta virus that circulates naturally in Argentina and Chile. Discover more Study Biology cruise Compare Boats Unlike most other strains of Hantavirus, which are transmitted to humans through rodents, the Andes strain can be transmitted directly from person to person. Check Symptoms By combining epidemiological data, contact history, and viral gene sequencing from laboratories in seven countries (Canada, France, the Netherlands , Senegal, South Africa, Spain, and Switzerland), scientists found a high degree of similarity in the viral genomes of patients on board the ship. Notably, one patient developed symptoms on May 31st – approximately 60 days after the ship left Argentina and following prolonged close contact with another infected person. You may also like Venezuela reports 3 deaths due to Hanta virus. Venezuela has confirmed three deaths from the Hanta virus, asserting that it is not transmitted from person to person, amid a complex global pandemic situation. The Ministry of Health provides an update on the Hanta virus outbreak on the cruise ship. (Dan Tri Newspaper) - The WHO has assessed that the outbreak of the Andean Hantavirus on the MV Hondius has been brought under control. However, the Ministry of Health still advises people to proactively take preventive measures. Vietnam has not recorded any cases of illness caused by the Hanta virus. According to the latest update from the World Health Organization, the Hanta virus outbreak linked to the MV Hondius cruise ship has been brought under control and no longer poses a public health risk. This period exceeds the 45-day incubation period used to assess the risk of infection before boarding, providing compelling evidence of transmission within the cruise ship. However, this is not a new or potentially mutated strain of the virus, but rather a strain already known for its human-to-human transmission. Check Symptoms In the second study, comparing the virus genome on the ship with historical samples from Argentina revealed a close genetic link to Andean strains previously detected near Villa Meliquina (Northern Patagonia) in 2018 and in Neuquén province between 2018 and 2025. This demonstrates that this virus strain had been circulating in the area for many years before the maritime incident. The investigative team also reconstructed the travel history of the first two patients – a couple who had traveled through Argentina and Chile before boarding the train but died before they could provide details. Immigration data showed they passed through the Icalma Pass (Argentina) 62 days before falling ill on April 3rd. Discover more Book Cruises Track Sea Cargo Find Treatments Because it exceeded the usual 45-day timeframe, this trip was deemed too early to pinpoint the exact location of initial exposure, even though genetic data had clarified the virus's evolutionary origins. Check Symptoms When viruses are transmitted between people for a short period, their genomes may differ by only 1 to 5 nucleotides (the building blocks of genetic material). To distinguish between actual viral mutations and technical errors, laboratories in seven countries, along with the World Health Organization (WHO), shared raw data and cross-referenced results. You may also like Dr. Gustavo Palacios, Professor of Microbiology at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai Health System (USA), said: "No single laboratory can tell the whole story on its own. Some groups know the history of viruses in South America, while others have strengths in epidemiological investigation, diagnosis, or genomic analysis. What makes the difference is the ability to combine those sources of knowledge, critically examine their own assumptions, and independently verify the evidence." Check Symptoms Agreeing with this assessment , Dr. Maria Van Kerkhove, Director of the WHO's Pandemic and Disease Management Division, emphasized that infectious diseases know no borders, and controlling them requires close cooperation, transparent information sharing, and sustained investment in preparedness, surveillance, laboratory networks, and emergency response. These two studies affirm that effective responses to global health emergencies depend on scientific networks, surveillance data, and historical patient samples that are maintained long-term prior to a crisis. This period exceeds the 45-day incubation period used to assess the risk of infection before boarding, providing compelling evidence of transmission within the cruise ship. However, this is not a new or potentially mutated strain of the virus, but rather a strain already known for its human-to-human transmission. Check Symptoms In the second study, comparing the virus genome on the ship with historical samples from Argentina revealed a close genetic link to Andean strains previously detected near Villa Meliquina (Northern Patagonia) in 2018 and in Neuquén province between 2018 and 2025. This demonstrates that this virus strain had been circulating in the area for many years before the maritime incident. The investigative team also reconstructed the travel history of the first two patients – a couple who had traveled through Argentina and Chile before boarding the train but died before they could provide details. Immigration data showed they passed through the Icalma Pass (Argentina) 62 days before falling ill on April 3rd. Discover more Book Cruises Track Sea Cargo Find Treatments Because it exceeded the usual 45-day timeframe, this trip was deemed too early to pinpoint the exact location of initial exposure, even though genetic data had clarified the virus's evolutionary origins. Check Symptoms When viruses are transmitted between people for a short period, their genomes may differ by only 1 to 5 nucleotides (the building blocks of genetic material). To distinguish between actual viral mutations and technical errors, laboratories in seven countries, along with the World Health Organization (WHO), shared raw data and cross-referenced results. You may also like Dr. Gustavo Palacios, Professor of Microbiology at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai Health System (USA), said: "No single laboratory can tell the whole story on its own. Some groups know the history of viruses in South America, while others have strengths in epidemiological investigation, diagnosis, or genomic analysis. What makes the difference is the ability to combine those sources of knowledge, critically examine their own assumptions, and independently verify the evidence." Check Symptoms Agreeing with this assessment , Dr. Maria Van Kerkhove, Director of the WHO's Pandemic and Disease Management Division, emphasized that infectious diseases know no borders, and controlling them requires close cooperation, transparent information sharing, and sustained investment in preparedness, surveillance, laboratory networks, and emergency response. These two studies affirm that effective responses to global health emergencies depend on scientific networks, surveillance data, and historical patient samples that are maintained long-term prior to a crisis. news.title: Orthohantaviruses Circulate Continuously in Argentine Wild Rodents Beyond Outbreak Periods
news.excerpt: Long-term surveillance in Argentina demonstrates that orthohantaviruses persist within diverse wild rodent populations even in the absence of documented human disease outbreaks.
news.rss_summary_html: Long-term surveillance in Argentina demonstrates that orthohantaviruses persist within diverse wild rodent populations even in the absence of documented human disease outbreaks.

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 27, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Orthohantaviruses Circulate Continuously in Argentine Wild Rodents Beyond Outbreak Periods by November 23, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 4 mins read 0 Orthohantaviruses Circulate Continuously in Argentine Wild Rodents Beyond Outbreak Periods Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Orthohantaviruses circulate continuously within wild rodent communities across Argentina during both outbreak and non-outbreak periods, according to an extensive scientific synthesis evaluating more than two decades of field investigations. While hantavirus pulmonary syndrome typically captures public concern only during acute epidemiological events, particularly when rare person-to-person transmission is confirmed, research demonstrates that viral activity persists uninterrupted in natural ecosystems. The pathogens do not disappear between recognized human epidemics; rather, they remain sustained within specialized wild sigmodontine rodent assemblages. Across these host populations, the virus does not infect every animal, but instead circulates steadily through a specific fraction of individuals, maintaining an unbroken transmission chain that operates independently of visible clinical clusters in human communities. Investigations conducted in Argentina for more than twenty years identify several sigmodontine rodent species as primary reservoirs of orthohantaviruses, with the majority belonging to the genus Oligoryzomys. The specific reservoir species responsible for viral maintenance vary substantially according to geographic region because individual Oligoryzomys species exhibit distinct regional distributions across the country. In southern Argentina, Oligoryzomys longicaudatus serves as the established primary reservoir host, whereas Oligoryzomys flavescens occupies that ecological role in the central region. In central and northeastern Argentina, Oligoryzomys nigripes acts as the dominant carrier, while Oligoryzomys chacoensis and Oligoryzomys occidentalis maintain circulation in the northwestern regions of the country, reflecting defined territorial boundaries among host species. Within these reservoir populations, transmission among wild rodents occurs horizontally rather than vertically from parent to offspring, creating distinct demographic patterns of infection. Because animals accumulate exposure over time, the statistical likelihood of an individual rodent contracting the virus increases progressively with age. Field surveys consistently demonstrate that adult males exhibit the highest infection rates among captured rodents. Researchers attribute this elevated prevalence primarily to frequent aggressive behavioral interactions among territorial adult males, although additional physiological factors may also contribute to heightened susceptibility or viral transmission efficiency. Consequently, viral circulation is maintained selectively within an active, mature demographic subpopulation rather than dispersing evenly across entire rodent communities. Each identified reservoir species is paired with a distinct orthohantavirus variant, shaping localized disease ecology and specific public health exposure risks. Transmission among rodents and transmission to humans both occur primarily through the inhalation of infectious aerosols generated from virus-contaminated rodent excreta. Human spillover infections typically arise under specific environmental conditions, such as entering poorly ventilated closed houses or storage structures where viral particles concentrate, or traversing dense vegetation where limited sunlight prevents viral degradation. Crucially, one specific regional variant, the Andes virus, possesses the proven capacity for person-to-person transmission, presenting a severe public health challenge that requires urgent, rapid response measures because human-to-human transmission is markedly more difficult to control than standard exposure to rodent droppings. Recent investigations demonstrate that orthohantavirus circulation in Argentina is not strictly confined to the genus Oligoryzomys, fundamentally revising traditional epidemiological paradigms. With the historical exception of Akodon azarae, in which infection was documented during earliest investigations, newer field surveys in central and northeastern Argentina have detected orthohantaviruses or reactive antibodies across multiple distinct genera. Detections now encompass Akodon species such as Akodon azarae and Akodon montensis, alongside Holochilus chacarius, Oxymycterus rufus, Scapteromys aquaticus, and Deltamys kempi. Notably, several of these newly identified viral detections involve distinct orthohantavirus variants that have not been associated with any confirmed human cases of hantavirus pulmonary syndrome to date. These expanded field discoveries encompass novel viral variants, the documentation of recognized orthohantaviruses in previously unrecorded host species, and the identification of lineages in Argentina that were formerly documented only in neighboring nations. Such evidence requires regular revisions to official taxonomic registries cataloging reservoir, host, and incidental host species. While these findings demonstrate that viral circulation is more geographically widespread and taxonomically diverse than previously recognized, scientists caution that apparent increases in prevalence partially reflect intensified sampling efforts and enhanced laboratory detection methods alongside potential ecological shifts. Furthermore, researchers emphasize that detecting antibodies alone does not definitively prove active viral maintenance, as it may merely reflect previous exposure through contact with primary reservoir species. Systematic surveillance expansion has likewise identified infected populations of established reservoir species across previously undocumented geographical locations. Consequently, the confirmed geographic distribution of orthohantaviruses is actively expanding alongside the recognized territorial boundaries of their host species. This ongoing geographic broadening requires healthcare providers across expanding catchment areas to remain vigilant for hantavirus pulmonary syndrome. Clinical teams must consider the disease when diagnosing patients who present with characteristic acute manifestations, such as high fever, severe muscle pain, and compatible clinical signs, even in regions historically perceived to have minimal viral transmission risk. Because orthohantavirus transmission persists during both outbreak and quiescent periods, health authorities stress that hantavirus pulmonary syndrome must not be underestimated in Argentina. The disease predominantly impacts individuals who live or work in rural or island environments where close contact with wild rodents occurs frequently. Although overall human incidence remains relatively low, the disease maintains a high case-fatality rate. In the absence of preventive vaccines, public health protection relies on continuous research, proactive epidemiological surveillance, extensive community education, and ongoing clinical training to ensure timely diagnosis and therapeutic response. While hantavirus pulmonary syndrome typically captures public concern only during acute epidemiological events, particularly when rare person-to-person transmission is confirmed, research demonstrates that viral activity persists uninterrupted in natural ecosystems. The pathogens do not disappear between recognized human epidemics; rather, they remain sustained within specialized wild sigmodontine rodent assemblages. Across these host populations, the virus does not infect every animal, but instead circulates steadily through a specific fraction of individuals, maintaining an unbroken transmission chain that operates independently of visible clinical clusters in human communities. Investigations conducted in Argentina for more than twenty years identify several sigmodontine rodent species as primary reservoirs of orthohantaviruses, with the majority belonging to the genus Oligoryzomys. The specific reservoir species responsible for viral maintenance vary substantially according to geographic region because individual Oligoryzomys species exhibit distinct regional distributions across the country. In southern Argentina, Oligoryzomys longicaudatus serves as the established primary reservoir host, whereas Oligoryzomys flavescens occupies that ecological role in the central region. In central and northeastern Argentina, Oligoryzomys nigripes acts as the dominant carrier, while Oligoryzomys chacoensis and Oligoryzomys occidentalis maintain circulation in the northwestern regions of the country, reflecting defined territorial boundaries among host species. Within these reservoir populations, transmission among wild rodents occurs horizontally rather than vertically from parent to offspring, creating distinct demographic patterns of infection. Because animals accumulate exposure over time, the statistical likelihood of an individual rodent contracting the virus increases progressively with age. Field surveys consistently demonstrate that adult males exhibit the highest infection rates among captured rodents. Researchers attribute this elevated prevalence primarily to frequent aggressive behavioral interactions among territorial adult males, although additional physiological factors may also contribute to heightened susceptibility or viral transmission efficiency. Consequently, viral circulation is maintained selectively within an active, mature demographic subpopulation rather than dispersing evenly across entire rodent communities. Each identified reservoir species is paired with a distinct orthohantavirus variant, shaping localized disease ecology and specific public health exposure risks. Transmission among rodents and transmission to humans both occur primarily through the inhalation of infectious aerosols generated from virus-contaminated rodent excreta. Human spillover infections typically arise under specific environmental conditions, such as entering poorly ventilated closed houses or storage structures where viral particles concentrate, or traversing dense vegetation where limited sunlight prevents viral degradation. Crucially, one specific regional variant, the Andes virus, possesses the proven capacity for person-to-person transmission, presenting a severe public health challenge that requires urgent, rapid response measures because human-to-human transmission is markedly more difficult to control than standard exposure to rodent droppings. Recent investigations demonstrate that orthohantavirus circulation in Argentina is not strictly confined to the genus Oligoryzomys, fundamentally revising traditional epidemiological paradigms. With the historical exception of Akodon azarae, in which infection was documented during earliest investigations, newer field surveys in central and northeastern Argentina have detected orthohantaviruses or reactive antibodies across multiple distinct genera. Detections now encompass Akodon species such as Akodon azarae and Akodon montensis, alongside Holochilus chacarius, Oxymycterus rufus, Scapteromys aquaticus, and Deltamys kempi. Notably, several of these newly identified viral detections involve distinct orthohantavirus variants that have not been associated with any confirmed human cases of hantavirus pulmonary syndrome to date. These expanded field discoveries encompass novel viral variants, the documentation of recognized orthohantaviruses in previously unrecorded host species, and the identification of lineages in Argentina that were formerly documented only in neighboring nations. Such evidence requires regular revisions to official taxonomic registries cataloging reservoir, host, and incidental host species. While these findings demonstrate that viral circulation is more geographically widespread and taxonomically diverse than previously recognized, scientists caution that apparent increases in prevalence partially reflect intensified sampling efforts and enhanced laboratory detection methods alongside potential ecological shifts. Furthermore, researchers emphasize that detecting antibodies alone does not definitively prove active viral maintenance, as it may merely reflect previous exposure through contact with primary reservoir species. Systematic surveillance expansion has likewise identified infected populations of established reservoir species across previously undocumented geographical locations. Consequently, the confirmed geographic distribution of orthohantaviruses is actively expanding alongside the recognized territorial boundaries of their host species. This ongoing geographic broadening requires healthcare providers across expanding catchment areas to remain vigilant for hantavirus pulmonary syndrome. Clinical teams must consider the disease when diagnosing patients who present with characteristic acute manifestations, such as high fever, severe muscle pain, and compatible clinical signs, even in regions historically perceived to have minimal viral transmission risk. Because orthohantavirus transmission persists during both outbreak and quiescent periods, health authorities stress that hantavirus pulmonary syndrome must not be underestimated in Argentina. The disease predominantly impacts individuals who live or work in rural or island environments where close contact with wild rodents occurs frequently. Although overall human incidence remains relatively low, the disease maintains a high case-fatality rate. In the absence of preventive vaccines, public health protection relies on continuous research, proactive epidemiological surveillance, extensive community education, and ongoing clinical training to ensure timely diagnosis and therapeutic response. analysis.brief_en: Orthohantaviruses are found continuously in wild rodent populations across Argentina, both during and outside of recognized human outbreak periods. This was established through over two decades of field research, revealing that these viruses persist in natural ecosystems without disappearing between epidemics. The primary reservoirs are various species of Oligoryzomys, with regional variations in which species dominate. In southern Argentina, Oligoryzomys longicaudatus is the main host, while Oligoryzomys flavescens is found in the central region, Oligoryzomys nigripes in central and northeastern areas, and Oligoryzomys chacoensis and Oligoryzomys occidentalis in the northwestern regions. The Andes virus, a specific variant, is notable for its ability to transmit between humans, making it a significant public health concern. Transmission occurs primarily through inhalation of aerosols from rodent excreta, and human infections typically happen under specific environmental conditions. The study underscores the need for updated taxonomic records and targeted public health strategies to address the localized risks posed by these viruses.

supplementary_news.title: 乡党们注意啦!出血热冬季流行期已至——防鼠灭鼠、疫苗接种、野外防护三道防线护平安
supplementary_news.excerpt: 秋风落尽,寒意渐浓,又到了出血热秋冬高发时段。肾综合征出血热或称流行性出血热,简称出血热,是由啮齿类动物主要是鼠类携带汉坦病毒引发人类感染的疾病,是我国法定传染病中的乙类传染病。田间村落、校园周边、郊外草丛,老鼠频繁往温暖处迁移,汉坦病毒藏在鼠粪鼠尿、分泌物里悄悄潜伏。它早期酷似感冒,极易被忽视,农民、学生、野外作业人员是重点防护人群。
